records.title: The Quran Presents the Book as Guidance

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Al-Baqarah answers the opening request for guidance by describing al-kitab as guidance for al-muttaqin.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Begins God → Revelation/Book → Guidance → Human Reception architecture.

records.title: Belief in Earlier Revelation Is Required

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The guided believers are described as believing both what was revealed to Muhammad and what was revealed before him.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Permanent evidence for QCA-0001; earlier revelation is positively affirmed.

records.title: Quranic Faith Includes Belief and Conduct

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The opening portrait of the guided includes unseen belief, prayer, giving, belief in revelation, belief in earlier revelation, and certainty of the Hereafter.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Supports emerging Faith → Worship → Conduct pattern without yet defining a complete salvation formula.

records.title: God Can Seal Human Receptivity

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The text attributes sealing of hearts and hearing to God and a covering over sight; the full causal relation between rejection and divine hardening remains open.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Compare later passages before deciding whether sealing precedes or judicially follows persistent rejection.

records.title: Spoken Profession Can Differ From Inner Belief

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Some claim belief in God and the Last Day while the text denies that they are believers.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Speech is not a sufficient indicator of genuine inner belief.

records.title: The Heart Has Moral/Spiritual Condition

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The heart is portrayed as sealable and diseased, showing qalb as an inner moral/spiritual faculty.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later 2:74 adds hardness, strengthening the pattern.

records.title: Humans Can Misperceive Their Moral Condition

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those causing corruption call themselves reformers while the Quran says they are corrupters who do not perceive it.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Establishes moral self-deception as a Quranic theme.

records.title: Creation Grounds God's Claim to Human Worship

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Humanity is commanded to worship its Lord because He created and sustains it and provides earth, sky, rain, and provision.

records.title: The Quran Appeals to an Inimitability Challenge

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Doubters are challenged to produce a surah comparable to what was sent down to God's servant.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The existence of the challenge is direct; whether it proves divine origin remains a separate research question.

records.title: Faith and Righteous Deeds Are Associated With Paradise

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers who do righteous deeds are promised gardens, strengthening the repeated faith-plus-conduct pattern.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Does not yet establish a complete merit-based salvation formula.

records.title: Humanity Receives a Distinctive Earthly Role

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God announces placement of a khalifah on earth; the exact semantic force of khalifah remains open.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not import 'vicegerent of God' without further lexical/contextual evidence.

records.title: Adam Receives Knowledge From God Beyond the Angels

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God teaches Adam the names; Adam can disclose them when the angels cannot.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Knowledge is presented as a divine gift connected to Adam's distinctive position.

records.title: Iblis' Rebellion Is Characterized by Refusal and Pride

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Iblis refuses the command to prostrate, acts arrogantly, and is counted among rejecters.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later jinn identification must be integrated before classifying any internal tension.

records.title: Adam and His Spouse Share the Transgression

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The passage addresses Adam and his spouse together and says Satan caused them to slip, without the Genesis sequence serpent → woman → man.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The spouse is unnamed in this passage; 'Eve/Hawwa' is extra-Quranic provenance here.

records.title: Adam Repents and God Accepts His Repentance

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Adam receives words from his Lord; God turns toward/accepts him in repentance and is called al-Tawwab al-Rahim.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fatalaqqa Adamu ... kalimatin; taba 'alayhi; al-Tawwab al-Rahim.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: No sacrifice, inherited guilt, or atoning mediator is mentioned here; absence in this verse is not yet a Quran-wide conclusion.

records.title: Divine Guidance Addresses Humanity's Post-Fall Condition

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After disobedience, repentance, and descent, God promises continuing guidance and ties final outcome to following or rejecting it.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Emerging architecture: creation → command → sin → repentance → mercy → earthly life → guidance → response → outcome.

records.title: The Quran Affirms a Prior Covenant With Israel

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The Children of Israel are commanded to remember God's favor and fulfill His covenant.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Israel is treated as having a genuine prior covenantal relationship with God.

records.title: The Quran Describes Its Revelation as Confirming What Israel Possesses

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The new revelation is described as confirming what is 'with you,' making this central evidence about the Quran's stance toward prior revelation.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Major evidence for QCA-0001; must be integrated with later accusations of concealment/distortion.

records.title: Concealment/False Mixing Is Not Automatically Textual Corruption

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The audience is accused of mixing truth with falsehood and knowingly concealing truth; the verse does not explicitly say Torah manuscripts were rewritten.

records.title: Possessing Scripture Does Not Guarantee Obedience

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: People are criticized for commanding righteousness while forgetting themselves even though they recite the Scripture.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Criticism concerns hypocrisy/disobedience, not denial that they possess Scripture.

records.title: The Quran Affirms Israel's Historical Divine Favor

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The Children of Israel are told God favored them over the worlds/peoples.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Emerging covenant logic: election/favor → obligation → accountability.

records.title: Golden-Calf Apostasy Is Followed by Divine Forgiveness

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After Israel takes the calf during Moses' forty nights, God says He pardoned them afterward.

records.title: The Quran Attributes Divine Scripture to Moses

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God says He gave Moses al-kitab and al-furqan so the people might be guided.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strong evidence that Mosaic revelation is treated as genuinely divine.

records.title: Golden-Calf Repentance Includes Severe Corporate Judgment

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Moses commands repentance after calf worship with language commonly rendered 'kill yourselves/one another'; exact scope and execution require further study.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Compare Exodus 32:25-29 and tafsir before final determination.

records.title: Some Israelites Substitute a Divine Instruction

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Wrongdoers are said to change/substitute the word they had been given in a specific entry/repentance command context.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: baddala alladhina zalamu qawlan ghayra alladhi qila lahum.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Relevant to QCA-0001 but does not by itself establish manuscript corruption of Torah.

records.title: 2:62 Gives a Positive Judgment Formula Including Jews and Christians

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse names believers, Jews, Christians, and Sabians, then states that whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness has reward with the Lord and no fear/grief.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: man amana billahi wal-yawmi al-akhiri wa-'amila salihan.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The text itself does not explicitly state the later interpretive limitation 'only before Muhammad'; QCA-0002 remains open.

records.title: Repeated Questioning Can Function as Resistance to Obedience

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: In the cow episode, a command to slaughter a cow is met with repeated requests for specifications before eventual compliance.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: Repeated qala ادع لنا ربك / questions over age, color, qualities.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Theme: revelation → response; questioning here appears to delay reluctant obedience.

records.title: The Quran Develops a Moral Anatomy of the Heart

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Across the opening of Al-Baqarah the heart can be sealed, diseased, and hardened, establishing qalb as a recurring moral/spiritual faculty.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strong cross-scriptural parallel with biblical hard-heart imagery.

records.title: Quran 2:75 Explicitly Accuses a Group of Deliberate Distortion

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A group is said to hear the speech/word of God, understand it, and then knowingly distort it.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: Key form: yuḥarrifūnahu, from ḥ-r-f; kalām Allāh is the object in context.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The accusation of deliberate distortion is direct; the mechanism (written alteration, oral change, interpretive misrepresentation, or another form) is not specified by this verse alone.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Major evidence for QCA-0001. Do not automatically translate the mechanism as wholesale manuscript corruption.

records.title: The Quran Distinguishes Scripture From People's Assumptions About It

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Some are described as not knowing the Book except amāniyy, while following conjecture.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-kitāb; amāniyy; semantic nuance of amāniyy remains open.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The verse distinguishes the Book from what some people merely suppose, wish, or recite without knowledge.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct Textual Statement; lexical nuance 🟠 open

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Supports the distinction between revelation itself and human assumptions about revelation.

records.title: The Quran Accuses Some People of Fabricating Religious Writing and Attributing It to God

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Some people are condemned for writing al-kitāb with their own hands and then saying 'This is from God' for a small gain.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: yaktubūna al-kitāba bi-aydīhim; hādhā min ʿindi Allāh.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Fabrication and false divine attribution are explicit. Scope is not defined as the entire Torah/Gospel textual tradition.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strong evidence for a fabrication category under QCA-0001; does not by itself prove wholesale corruption.

records.title: Religious Presumption Does Not Guarantee Salvation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A claim that punishment will last only a limited number of days is challenged; final outcomes are tied to evil/sin versus belief and righteous deeds.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: Relevant terms include sayyiʾah, khaṭīʾah, īmān, and ʿamal ṣāliḥ.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The text rejects unsupported confidence in limited punishment and contrasts Fire with Paradise.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Religious identity or presumption is not presented as sufficient security.

records.title: Quran 2:85 Accuses People of Selective Acceptance and Rejection of Scripture

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The text criticizes people for believing in part of the Book and rejecting another part while violating covenant obligations.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Selective acceptance/rejection is explicit and must remain distinct from textual alteration.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Adds a separate corruption/mishandling category to QCA-0001.

records.title: Jesus Is Positively Presented as a Divinely Supported Messenger

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Jesus son of Mary is given clear signs and strengthened with the Holy Spirit within the succession of messengers.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam; al-bayyināt; rūḥ al-qudus.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The positive divine support is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: First canonical Jesus dossier entry. Does not yet settle divinity, sonship, crucifixion, or Gospel questions.

records.title: Jesus Is Strengthened by Rūḥ al-Qudus

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The Quran explicitly associates Jesus with rūḥ al-qudus.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: rūḥ al-qudus (روح القدس), literally Spirit of Holiness/Holy Spirit.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The phrase is direct; identification with Gabriel is not made explicitly in 2:87.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later Islamic identification with Gabriel must be distinguished from Quranic wording and tested against internal evidence.

records.title: Resistance to Revelation Is Again Located in the Inner Person

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The audience speaks of hearts being ghulf; the Quran frames their condition in relation to rejection.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The heart continues as the locus of receptivity/rejection.

records.title: The Quran Again Claims to Confirm Existing Earlier Revelation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A Book from God is described as confirming what is with them, yet some reject it.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Confirmation of what is possessed by the addressed community is explicit.

records.title: The Quran's Criticism Presupposes Continuing Relevance of Earlier Revelation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The audience claims belief in what was revealed to them while rejecting later revelation that the Quran describes as true and confirming what is with them.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The argument treats prior revelation as sufficiently meaningful for a confirmation argument.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Supports a nuanced rather than total-loss model at this stage.

records.title: Claims of Exclusive Religious Privilege Are Subjected to Moral Testing

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Exclusive claims about the final home with God are challenged, and attachment to life is used rhetorically against unsupported confidence.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: Relevant salvation/judgment vocabulary; no special new lexical item required.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The Quran rejects mere communal presumption as proof of eschatological privilege.

records.title: Gabriel Is Explicitly Identified as an Agent of Quranic Revelation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Gabriel brings revelation to the messenger's heart by God's permission; Michael is also named.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Gabriel's role as revelatory agent is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Creates an internal comparison question with rūḥ al-qudus but does not yet establish identity.

records.title: Quran 2:101 Describes People of Scripture as Disregarding the Book of God

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A group from those given Scripture throws the Book of God behind their backs when a confirming messenger comes.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The text criticizes disregard of something it calls the Book of God.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important evidence against assuming the Quran depicts all prior Scripture as wholly unusable at this point.

records.title: The Quran Explicitly Exonerates Solomon From Disbelieving Magic

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The text states that Solomon did not disbelieve; rather, the devils disbelieved and taught people magic.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: wa-mā kafara Sulaymān wa-lākinna al-shayāṭīna kafarū; siḥr.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Suggests engagement with a tradition associating Solomon and magic; source/history investigation required.

records.title: The Quran Treats Magic as Potentially Effective but Subordinate to God

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: People learn practices capable of separating spouses, yet cannot harm anyone except by God's permission.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The narrative treats harmful supernatural efficacy as possible but limited by divine sovereignty.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct Textual Statement within narrative worldview

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Historical demonstrability of supernatural causation remains separate from what the text claims.

records.title: Harut and Marut Require Dedicated Interpretive Investigation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Harut and Marut are associated with Babylon and, in the standard reading, with the two angels; they warn that they are a trial and not to disbelieve.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: Hārūt, Mārūt, Bābil, al-malakayn in the standard reading.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Identity, syntax, and interpretive history are disputed.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Requires classical tafsir, qirāʾāt/syntax, and Late Antique source investigation.

records.title: The Quran Regulates How Believers Address the Messenger

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are told not to use rāʿinā but to use unẓurnā and listen.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The speech regulation is direct; the precise reason for the replacement is not self-evident from the verse alone.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later wordplay/insult explanations belong to tafsir provenance unless independently established.

records.title: Quran 2:106 Introduces Replacement/Abrogation Language

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The text speaks of naskh or causing an āyah to be forgotten and bringing one better or similar.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Replacement/abrogation language is direct; the precise scope of āyah and whether Quranic verses are specifically in view remains open.

records.title: Quran 2:111 Rejects Mere Communal Identity as Proof of Salvation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Exclusive Jewish/Christian claims to Paradise are called unsupported wishes and challenged with 'bring your proof.'

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The rejection of communal-identity proof is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Reinforces earlier rejection of inherited or communal presumption.

records.title: Quran 2:112 Links Submission to God and Good Conduct With Reward

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Whoever submits his face/self to God while doing good is promised reward and no fear/grief.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Submission and doing good are explicitly tied to positive judgment language.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important for QCA-0002; does not yet settle later requirement of explicit acceptance of Muhammad.

records.title: Jews and Christians Are Depicted as Mutually Rejecting One Another While Both Recite Scripture

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse reports reciprocal Jewish-Christian claims that the other stands on nothing, while both recite the Book.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Mutual denunciation and recitation of Scripture are explicit.

records.title: God's Sovereignty Is Not Spatially Confined

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: East and west belong to God; wherever one turns is the wajh of God.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Universal divine sovereignty is direct; exact theology of 'face' remains open.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct Textual Statement; anthropomorphic semantics 🟠 open

records.title: The Quran Explicitly Rejects the Claim That God Has Taken a Son

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The Quran rejects the proposition that God has taken a son and grounds the rejection in divine transcendence, ownership, and creative command.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ittakhadha Allāhu waladan; subḥānahu; kun fa-yakūn.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Rejection of divine sonship is explicit; Jesus is not named in this verse.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Opened QB-0028. Later passages must determine whether Quranic rejection accurately represents Christian sonship doctrine.

records.title: Quran 2:121 Recognizes Proper/True Recitation of the Book

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those given the Book who recite it with its due/true recitation are positively distinguished.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The possibility of proper recitation is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important evidence against a simplistic total-unavailability model.

records.title: Abraham Is Presented as a Universal Religious Leader

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After Abraham completes divine tests, God says He will make him an imam for humanity.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Abraham's universal leadership role is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Extends Abraham beyond merely Israelite ancestry.

records.title: Descent From Abraham Does Not Automatically Guarantee Covenant Status

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God's covenant is said not to reach the wrongdoers among Abraham's descendants.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Mere descent is insufficient for covenant inclusion.

records.title: The Quran Associates Abraham and Ishmael Jointly With Raising the Foundations of the Sacred House

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Abraham and Ishmael are depicted raising the foundations of the House and praying together.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Major narrative addition versus Genesis; historical-source investigation required.

records.title: Abraham and Ishmael Pray for a Future Messenger Among Their Descendants

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: They pray for a messenger from among them who will recite signs, teach Book and wisdom, and purify.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The prayer for a future messenger is explicit; identity is not named in the verse.

records.title: Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob Are Presented Within One Monotheistic Line

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Jacob's descendants affirm worship of the God of Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ilāhaka wa-ilāha ābāʾika Ibrāhīma wa-Ismāʿīla wa-Isḥāqa.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The Quran integrates Ishmael into the patriarchal theological line.

records.title: Ancestral Merit Does Not Transfer Automatically

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Past communities receive what they earned, and later people receive what they earn.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: lahā mā kasabat wa-lakum mā kasabtum.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Accountability is explicitly non-transferable between communities.

records.title: The Quran Claims Continuity Across Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Other Prophets

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are instructed to affirm revelation given to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, tribes, Moses, Jesus, and the prophets.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: āmannā ... wa-mā ūtiya Mūsā wa-ʿĪsā ... lā nufarriqu.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The Quran presents itself as continuity/restoration rather than rejection of prior prophets.

records.title: The Quran Explicitly Changes an Earlier Prayer Direction

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The believers are turned away from a previous qiblah and instructed to face al-Masjid al-Haram.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: A former religious practice and a new mandated practice are both explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strong concrete evidence that divine legislation/practice can change.

records.title: The Former Qiblah Is Presented as a Test of Loyalty

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The earlier qiblah is described as serving to distinguish those who follow the messenger from those who turn back.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The change is framed as deliberate testing, not divine correction of error.

records.title: The Quran Assigns the Believing Community a Witness Role

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The community is called ummatan wasaṭan so that it may be witnesses over humanity, with the messenger witness over it.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Witness role is direct; semantic force of wasaṭ remains open.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct Textual Statement; lexical nuance 🟠 open

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not reduce wasaṭ automatically to modern 'moderate'.

records.title: Quranic Continuity Does Not Mean Identical Religious Practice

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The text acknowledges different qiblah directions among communities while maintaining the Quran's continuity claims.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Helps distinguish theological continuity from identical law/ritual.

records.title: The Quran Again Accuses a Group Among People of Scripture of Knowing and Concealing Truth

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those given the Book are said to recognize the relevant truth as they recognize their sons, while a group knowingly conceals truth.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Concealment is explicit; precise antecedent of the pronoun requires careful context analysis.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Adds another concealment category item to QCA-0001.

records.title: The Quran Urges Competition in Good Works Amid Ritual Difference

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After discussing differing directions, the Quran tells communities to race toward good deeds.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The exhortation to good works is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Prepares the stronger statement in 2:177 that righteousness exceeds directional ritual.

records.title: Quran 2:151 Presents the Messenger as Fulfilling Functions Requested in Abraham's Prayer

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The messenger recites signs, purifies, teaches the Book and wisdom—the same functions requested by Abraham and Ishmael.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strengthens Quran-internal identification of the prayed-for messenger.

records.title: Human Remembrance of God Is Met by Divine Remembrance

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God commands remembrance and says He will remember those who remember Him.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Adds relational reciprocity to worship theology.

records.title: The Quran Claims Those Killed in God's Way Possess Continuing Life

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those killed in the way of God are not to be called dead; they are alive though humans do not perceive.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Continuing life is direct; exact state is undefined here.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Requires later integration with resurrection/intermediate-state teaching.

records.title: Earthly Suffering Functions as Divine Testing

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Fear, hunger, losses, and hardship are described as tests, with patient believers responding that they belong to God and return to Him.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: la-nabluwannakum; ṣabr; innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūn.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Parallels qiblah change as a loyalty/response test.

records.title: Ṣafā and Marwah Are Incorporated Into Quranic Pilgrimage

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Ṣafā and Marwah are called among God's ritual symbols, and pilgrimage/ʿumrah passage between them is permitted/recognized.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-Ṣafā; al-Marwah; shaʿāʾir Allāh; ḥajja; iʿtamara.

records.title: Concealment of Revelation Is Reversible Through Repentance, Reform, and Disclosure

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those who conceal clear proofs and guidance are condemned, except those who repent, reform, and make clear.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Concealment and its corrective disclosure are explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important evidence that some corruption accusations concern concealment of existing truth, not loss of text.

records.title: Quranic Monotheism Is Explicitly Exclusive

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The Quran declares one God and no deity except Him, again using al-Rahman al-Rahim.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ilāhukum ilāhun wāḥid; lā ilāha illā huwa.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Creates strong agreement with biblical one-God affirmation while Trinity compatibility remains a later question.

records.title: Creation Functions as Signs Pointing Toward God

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Cosmic and natural phenomena are called āyāt for people who reason.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Demonstrates āyah has a semantic range broader than 'Quranic verse,' relevant to QCA-0003.

records.title: Idolatry Includes Misplaced Ultimate Allegiance and Love

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Some take rivals beside God and love them as God should be loved; believers are stronger in love for God.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The text treats ultimate love/allegiance toward rivals as a form of theological error.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Will connect to later shirk research.

records.title: Ancestral Tradition Is Not Sufficient Religious Authority

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: People who prefer inherited ancestral practice over revelation are criticized even if their ancestors lacked understanding or guidance.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: mā alfaynā ʿalayhi ābāʾanā; lā yaʿqilūna; lā yahtadūn.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The rejection of ancestry as sufficient authority is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Consistent with rejection of inherited merit and communal presumption.

records.title: Quranic Food Law Includes a Necessity Exception

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Carrion, blood, pork, and food dedicated to other than God are prohibited, with an exception for compelled necessity without deliberate transgression.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Prohibition and necessity exception are explicit.

records.title: Material Gain Is Presented as a Motive for Concealing Revelation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those who conceal what God revealed in the Book and exchange it for a small price are condemned.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: yaktumūna mā anzala Allāhu min al-kitāb; thamanan qalīlan.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Concealment for material gain is explicit.

records.title: Ritual Correctness Alone Does Not Constitute Righteousness

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse explicitly says righteousness is not merely turning faces east or west.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: laysa al-birra an tuwallū wujūhakum qibala al-mashriqi wa-l-maghrib.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The limitation of directional ritual as a definition of righteousness is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important theological clarification immediately after qiblah controversy.

records.title: Quranic Righteousness Integrates Belief, Worship, Ethics, Generosity, Covenant Fidelity, and Perseverance

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse defines birr through belief in God, Last Day, angels, Book and prophets; generosity; prayer; almsgiving; covenant fulfillment; and patience.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-birr; āman; ātā al-māla; aqāma al-ṣalāh; ātā al-zakāh; al-mūfūna bi-ʿahdihim; al-ṣābirīn.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The integrated character of righteousness is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Strongest Quranic summary of religious life encountered so far.

records.title: The Quran Establishes Regulated Retaliation for Homicide

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Retaliation (qiṣāṣ) is prescribed in homicide cases, while forgiveness/compensation is also allowed and the stated purpose includes preservation of life.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The legal framework directly combines proportional retaliation with an avenue of forgiveness/compensation.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Retaliation is regulated rather than unlimited private vengeance.

records.title: Quran 2:178 Uses Social-Status and Sex Categories in Its Retaliation Formula

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse states free for free, slave for slave, and female for female in its qiṣāṣ formula.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-ḥurru bil-ḥurri; al-ʿabdu bil-ʿabdi; al-unthā bil-unthā.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The wording is explicit; whether it equalizes liability, restricts cross-status retaliation, or responds to tribal excess requires legal/historical study.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not erase the asymmetrical/status wording or prematurely impose later fiqh explanations.

records.title: Quran 2:180 Prescribes a Bequest for Parents and Near Relatives

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A bequest is prescribed when death approaches a person with wealth, with condemnation of improper alteration and allowance for corrective reconciliation where injustice is feared.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The bequest command is explicit. Its relationship to later inheritance shares in Surah 4 remains open.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Future comparison with Surah 4 is mandatory under QCA-0003.

records.title: The Quran Claims Fasting Continuity With Earlier Communities

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Fasting is prescribed for believers as it was prescribed for those before them, with taqwā stated as a purpose.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: kutiba ʿalaykumu al-ṣiyāmu kamā kutiba ʿalā alladhīna min qablikum.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Continuity of fasting practice is explicit; identity of earlier regulations is not specified.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not equate generic fasting continuity with an identical earlier Ramadan law.

records.title: Ramadan Is Connected to the Sending Down of the Quran

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Ramadan is identified as the month in which the Quran was sent down, described as guidance and clear proofs/criterion.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: shahru Ramaḍān; unzila fīhi al-Qurʾān; hudan; furqān.

records.title: Quranic Fasting Law Contains Explicit Hardship Exceptions

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Illness and travel permit later replacement days, and the text states that God intends ease rather than hardship.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: marīḍan; ʿalā safarin; yurīdu Allāhu bikumu al-yusr.

records.title: The Quran Presents God as Directly Accessible in Prayer

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God says He is near and responds to the caller when called.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Direct divine nearness/response language is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: No human mediator is specified in this verse.

records.title: Ramadan Fasting Is a Daily Dawn-to-Night Fast

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Eating, drinking, and marital relations are permitted at night; abstention runs from dawn until night.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-khayṭ al-abyaḍ/min al-khayṭ al-aswad; atimmū al-ṣiyāma ilā al-layl.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Clarifies the nature of the Ramadan fast.

records.title: Marriage Is Described Through Reciprocal Garment Imagery

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Spouses are described reciprocally as garments for one another.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: hunna libāsun lakum wa-antum libāsun lahunna.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Must be integrated with later asymmetrical family-law passages.

records.title: The Quran Condemns Using Authorities to Obtain Others’ Wealth Wrongfully

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are forbidden to consume wealth wrongfully and to use it with authorities/judges to obtain others’ property knowingly.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: tudlū bihā ilā al-ḥukkām; taʾkulū amwāla al-nāsi bil-ithm.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Commercial/legal integrity is part of religious ethics.

records.title: The Quran Uses Lunar Cycles as Religious Time Markers

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: New moons are described as time markers for people and pilgrimage.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Also rejects a ritual/custom as constituting righteousness by itself.

records.title: Quran 2:190 Authorizes Fighting Those Who Fight Believers While Prohibiting Transgression

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are commanded to fight in God’s way those who fight them and not transgress.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Combat authorization and anti-transgression limit are explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: At this canonical point, the object is those fighting the believers.

records.title: “Kill Them Wherever You Find Them” Occurs Within an Existing Warfare/Expulsion Context

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The killing command follows 2:190’s combat context and 2:191 refers to expulsion and fighting at the Sacred Mosque only if opponents fight there.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: uqtulūhum ḥaythu thaqiftumūhum; akhrijūhum min ḥaythu akhrajūkum.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Contextual linkage is direct; the verse still authorizes killing enemy forces in the described conflict.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Reject both decontextualized universalization and sanitization of the lethal command.

records.title: Quran 2:192-193 Places a Cessation Condition on Warfare

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: If opponents cease, aggression is to cease except against wrongdoers; fighting is linked to ending fitnah.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fa-in intahaw; lā ʿudwāna illā ʿalā al-ẓālimīn; fitnah.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Cessation condition is explicit; exact meaning of fitnah requires lexical/contextual study.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct Textual Statement; FITNAH scope 🟠 open

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Critical for later full warfare corpus analysis.

records.title: Quranic Warfare Retaliation Is Explicitly Limited by Proportionality

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A response to aggression is authorized only in proportion to the aggression suffered.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fa-man iʿtadā ʿalaykum faʿtadū ʿalayhi bi-mithli mā iʿtadā ʿalaykum.

records.title: The Quran Explicitly Warns Against Self-Destruction

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are told not to throw themselves into destruction by their own hands.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Warning is explicit; broader suicide doctrine is not established from this verse alone.

records.title: Quranic Pilgrimage Combines Ritual Performance With Moral Discipline

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Hajj/ʿumrah regulations are paired with restrictions on sexual misconduct, wrongdoing, quarrelling, and commands to remember God.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ḥajj; ʿumrah; rafath; fusūq; jidāl; dhikr.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Ritual and moral requirements are explicitly joined.

records.title: The Quran Does Not Require Pilgrimage to Be Economically Isolated

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Seeking bounty/provision during pilgrimage is explicitly permitted.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Religious pilgrimage and legitimate commerce can coexist.

records.title: The Quran Rejects a Purely This-Worldly Religious Orientation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The preferred prayer seeks good in this world, good in the Hereafter, and protection from the Fire.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ḥasanatan fī al-dunyā; ḥasanatan fī al-ākhirah.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Rejects both purely worldly and purely world-denying orientation.

records.title: Persuasive Religious Speech Can Conceal a Corrupt Inner Condition

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A person’s impressive speech and appeal to God as witness can coexist with hostility and destructive conduct.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: yuʿjibuka qawluhu; yushhidu Allāha ʿalā mā fī qalbihi.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Contrast between speech and inner/moral reality is explicit.

records.title: Quran 2:208 Calls for Comprehensive Submission/Peace Rather Than Partial Allegiance

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are told to enter al-silm completely and not follow Satan’s steps.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Comprehensive entry is direct; exact nuance of al-silm remains lexical.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not assume the noun is identical in form to later technical “Islam” without lexical note.

records.title: The Quran Explains Religious Disagreement as Arising After Genuine Revelation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God sends prophets and the Book in truth to judge disputes; disagreement then arises among recipients.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Genuine revelation preceding human disagreement is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Important against models that deny genuine earlier revelation existed.

records.title: Entry Into Paradise Is Associated With Perseverance Through Severe Testing

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are warned to expect hardship like prior communities before entering Paradise.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: No atoning function of suffering is established here.

records.title: Quranic Charity Prioritizes Concrete Human Relationships and Vulnerability

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Spending priorities include parents, relatives, orphans, needy people, and travelers.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-wālidayn; al-aqrabīn; al-yatāmā; al-masākīn; ibn al-sabīl.

records.title: Some Divine Commands Are Presented as Contrary to Human Preference

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Fighting is prescribed despite believers’ aversion; humans may dislike what is good and love what is harmful.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: kutiba ʿalaykumu al-qitāl; ʿasā an takrahū.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Divine knowledge is presented as superior to human preference.

records.title: Quran 2:217 Condemns Apostasy Spiritually but Does Not Here Prescribe an Earthly Death Penalty

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those who turn back from religion and die in rejection have works nullified and face eschatological punishment.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: yartadid minkum ʿan dīnihi fa-yamut wa-huwa kāfir.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Spiritual/eschatological consequence is explicit; no earthly execution command occurs in this verse.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later hadith/fiqh must remain separate provenance.

records.title: Quran 2:219 Condemns Intoxicants and Gambling Without Yet Issuing an Explicit Absolute Prohibition

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Khamr and maysir are said to contain great sin and some benefits, with sin greater than benefit.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Moral condemnation is explicit; absolute prohibition wording is not yet present.

records.title: Quran 2:221 Prohibits Marriage Between Believers and Polytheists

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Believers are forbidden to marry mushrik women until they believe, and believing women are not to be given to mushrik men.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The polytheist marriage prohibition is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Does not by itself settle marriage with Jews/Christians; 5:5 remains future evidence.

records.title: Quran 2:222 Prohibits Sexual Intercourse During Menstruation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Menstruation is called adhā and sexual approach is prohibited until purification.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-maḥīḍ; adhā; lā taqrabūhunna ḥattā yaṭhurna.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Sexual prohibition is explicit; social isolation is not established by this verse alone.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Compare with broader Torah impurity system.

records.title: Quran 2:223 Uses Fertility/Agricultural Imagery for Marital Sexual Relations

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Wives are described as ḥarth (tilth/cultivation) and husbands are told to approach their cultivation.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Agricultural/reproductive metaphor is direct; exact sexual-law scope requires context/tafsir analysis.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Must be read with reciprocal garment imagery in 2:187 and later family law.

records.title: Oaths Do Not Override the Obligation to Do Good

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God’s name in oaths must not become an obstacle to righteousness, taqwā, or reconciliation; careless oaths are distinguished from heart intention.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Priority of righteousness over oath misuse is explicit.

records.title: Quranic Law Limits Indefinite Marital Sexual Abandonment

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Men who swear abstinence from wives receive a four-month period after which reconciliation or divorce must be resolved.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: yuʾlūna min nisāʾihim; tarabbuṣu arbaʿati ashhur.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Prevents indefinite limbo through abstinence oath.

records.title: Quran 2:228 Affirms Reciprocal Marital Rights and Responsibilities

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Women are said to have rights corresponding in recognized manner to obligations upon them.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Must remain alongside male darajah statement in same verse.

records.title: Quran 2:228 Assigns Men a “Degree” Over Women in the Divorce/Marriage Context

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After reciprocal-rights language, the verse states that men have a darajah over women.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The asymmetry is explicit; scope and meaning remain cumulative.

records.title: Quran 2:229 Limits Revocable Divorce and Commands Humane Retention or Release

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Divorce is twice, after which spouses are to be retained honorably or released with kindness; compensation-based separation is also contemplated.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: al-ṭalāqu marratān; imsākun bi-maʿrūf aw tasrīḥun bi-iḥsān.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Limits and humane alternatives are explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Designed against endless abusive cycles of divorce/return.

records.title: After the Final Divorce, Immediate Remarriage to the First Husband Is Prohibited

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: After a further/final divorce, remarriage to the first husband is not lawful until a genuine marriage to another husband has occurred and ended.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: lā taḥillu lahu min baʿdu ḥattā tankiḥa zawjan ghayrahu.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The Quran does not command a sham “halalah” marriage.

records.title: Quranic Divorce Law Prohibits Using Reconciliation as a Tool of Harm

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Men are forbidden to retain women in order to harm or transgress.

records.title: Quran 2:232 Recognizes a Divorced Woman’s Role in Consenting to Remarriage

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Others are told not to block former spouses from remarrying when they mutually agree honorably.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later guardian law must not erase the verse’s mutual-consent wording.

records.title: Quran 2:233 Creates Reciprocal Parental Obligations Around Breastfeeding

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Mothers may nurse two full years; fathers owe reasonable support; neither parent is to be harmed; early weaning can occur by mutual consultation.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ḥawlayni kāmilayn; rizquhunna wa-kiswatuhunna; tarāḍin wa-tashāwur.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Reciprocal duties and consultation are explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Combines maternal nursing role, paternal support, non-harm, and consultation.

records.title: Quranic Widowhood Law Establishes a Four-Month-and-Ten-Day Waiting Period

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Widows wait four months and ten days before remarriage; indirect proposals are allowed but secret contracts are not.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Waiting period is explicit; rationale is not specified in the verse.

records.title: Quranic Divorce Law Protects Financial Interests Even Before Consummation

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Divorce before consummation still carries provision obligations, including half the specified dower where fixed unless waived.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Marriage is treated as carrying enforceable financial duties.

records.title: Quranic Prayer Obligation Adapts to Dangerous Circumstances

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Prayer is to be guarded, but danger permits prayer while walking or riding.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Adaptive form under danger is explicit.

records.title: Quran 2 Contains Both a Four-Month-Ten-Day Widow Waiting Period and a One-Year Widow Provision

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The surah states a four-month-ten-day waiting period and separately a one-year provision/residence statement for widows.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: arbaʿata ashhurin wa-ʿashran; matāʿan ilā al-ḥawli.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Both provisions are explicit; their legal relationship remains open.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Potentially different subjects, complementary rules, or legislative development; later Surah 4 required.

records.title: Quran 2:241 Recognizes Financial Provision for Divorced Women

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Reasonable provision for divorced women is described as a duty upon the God-conscious.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Must remain part of any overall evaluation of Quranic divorce rights.

records.title: The Quran Presents a Collective Death-and-Revival Event

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A large group leaves homes fearing death; God causes them to die and then revives them.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fa-qāla lahumu Allāhu mūtū thumma aḥyāhum.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: The narrative presents actual death/revival; historical identity is unspecified.

fields.label: Evidence classification
fields.value: 🟢 Direct narrative claim; historical identification 🟠 open

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not classify false merely because supernatural; historical verification remains separate.

records.title: Divine Selection of Tālūt Is Not Based on Wealth or Social Prestige

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Tālūt is chosen as king despite objections about wealth/status; selection is tied to knowledge and bodily capacity.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: ṭalūta malikan; basṭatan fī al-ʿilmi wa-l-jism.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Reinforces divine versus human status criteria.

records.title: The Quran Associates Tālūt’s Kingship With the Return of the Ark

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The sign of Tālūt’s kingship is the coming of the tābūt containing sakīnah and remnants from Moses/Aaron families, carried by angels.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Major narrative addition requiring source investigation.

records.title: David Is Presented as Goliath’s Slayer and Recipient of Kingship and Wisdom

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: David kills Jālūt; God gives him kingship, wisdom, and further teaching.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: qatala Dāwūdu Jālūta; ātāhu Allāhu al-mulka wa-l-ḥikmah.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Core event and gifts are explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Core agreement with 1 Samuel 17 amid broader narrative rearrangement.

records.title: The Quran Affirms Unequal Rank Among Messengers

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God favors some messengers over others while Jesus is again named with clear signs and Holy Spirit support.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: faḍḍalnā baʿḍahum ʿalā baʿḍ; rafʿa baʿḍahum darajāt.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Can coexist with “make no distinction” in accepting all messengers; no QI yet.

records.title: Quran 2:255 Gives the Most Concentrated Divine-Attribute Statement So Far

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God is the only deity, Ever-Living, Sustainer, sleepless, sovereign, omniscient, unwearied in preserving creation, and Most High/Great.

records.title: Intercession Exists Only by God’s Permission

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse denies intercession apart from God’s permission.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: man dhā alladhī yashfaʿu ʿindahu illā bi-idhnihi.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: The Quran does not deny intercession absolutely here; it subordinates it to divine permission.

records.title: Quran 2:256 Explicitly States “No Compulsion in Religion”

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: The verse states lā ikrāha fī al-dīn and contrasts right guidance with error.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: lā ikrāha fī al-dīn; rushd; ghayy.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Must be integrated with later warfare, jizyah, apostasy, and legal texts rather than erased or absolutized prematurely.

records.title: Guidance Is Repeatedly Framed as Movement From Darkness Into Light

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: God brings believers from darkness into light; false powers reverse that movement.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Light/darkness guidance metaphor is explicit and recurrent.

records.title: Quran 2:258 Narrates Abraham Defeating an Unnamed King in Theological Debate

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Abraham argues from God’s power over life/death and sunrise; the opponent is confounded.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: alladhī ḥājja Ibrāhīma fī rabbihi; fa-buhita.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Debate narrative is explicit; ruler is unnamed.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later identification as Nimrod is extra-Quranic provenance.

records.title: Quran 2:259 Presents a Hundred-Year Death-and-Revival Sign

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: An unnamed man is caused to die for one hundred years and then revived in a resurrection demonstration.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fa-amātahu Allāhu miʾata ʿāmin thumma baʿathahu.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Death/revival narrative is explicit; identity unspecified.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Later identification such as Ezra must be kept extra-Quranic unless textually established.

records.title: The Quran Distinguishes Faith From Desire for Confirmatory Evidence

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Abraham says he believes but asks to see how God gives life to the dead so his heart may be reassured.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Belief plus request for reassurance is explicit.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Seeking reassurance is not portrayed here as unbelief.

records.title: Quranic Charity Is Evaluated by Motive and Treatment of the Recipient, Not Amount Alone

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Charity is multiplied when sincere; reminders, injury, showmanship, and inferior giving can destroy moral value.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Motive/dignity conditions recur throughout the section.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Giving and recipient dignity are inseparable in the ethical evaluation.

records.title: Quran 2:275-279 Explicitly Prohibits Ribā While Distinguishing It From Trade

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Trade is permitted and ribā forbidden; believers are ordered to abandon outstanding ribā.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Trade/ribā distinction and prohibition are explicit; precise economic scope of ribā remains historical/legal research.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Do not automatically map ribā to every modern interest arrangement without analysis.

records.title: Persistent Ribā Is Condemned With Exceptionally Severe Language

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Those who refuse to abandon outstanding ribā are warned of war from God and His Messenger.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Places exploitative/forbidden lending in a severe moral category.

records.title: Quranic Debt Law Requires Forbearance Toward an Insolvent Debtor

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: A debtor in hardship is to receive postponement until ease; forgiveness is commended as better.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: fa-naẓiratun ilā maysarah; an taṣaddaqū khayrun lakum.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Forbearance and debt forgiveness are explicit.

records.title: Quran 2:282 Establishes Detailed Written-Contract Safeguards for Deferred Debt

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: Deferred debts are to be written with just scribal procedure, defined term, debtor dictation/guardian help, witnesses, and protections for scribes/witnesses.

fields.value: dayn; ajal musammā; kātib bil-ʿadl; shuhadāʾ.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward

records.title: Quran 2:282 Uses a One-Man/Two-Women Witness Formula for Deferred Debt Contracts

fields.label: Discovery statement
fields.value: For the specified debt transaction, two men are preferred; if unavailable, one man and two women are specified so one may remind the other if she errs/forgets.

fields.label: Original-language evidence
fields.value: rajulayni; rajulun wa-imraʾatāni; an taḍilla iḥdāhumā fa-tudhakkira iḥdāhumā al-ukhrā.

fields.label: Supporting evidence
fields.value: Gendered formula and rationale are explicit in this transaction context.

fields.label: Explanation / carry-forward
fields.value: Does not by itself prove a universal half-value rule for women’s testimony in every case.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP01 vv001-020
paragraphs: Canonical position: Surah 2 of 114; verses 1–20 of 286
Traditional chronology: Medinan (surah as a whole). Opening block is widely treated as Medinan prologue. Certainty: traditional classification of the surah; this block is not internally dated.
Why this cut: Natural rhetorical close: three human types + two parables (fire/rain). v.21 begins a new address: “O mankind, worship your Lord.”

Al-Baqarah is the longest Quranic surah. This checkpoint covers only the opening twenty verses. The block does three things: (1) presents “the Book” as undoubted guidance for the God-conscious; (2) defines that group by unseen-faith, prayer, spending, belief in what was sent down to “you” and before you, and certainty of the hereafter; (3) contrasts two failing groups — those who disbelieve and will not believe even if warned, and people who say they believe but do not — then closes with two parables.

The word munāfiqūn (hypocrites) does not appear in 2:8–20. Classical tafsir almost unanimously reads 8–20 as the Medinan hypocrites. That identification is Level 3–4 unless later Quranic usage inside this project ties the same portrait to the named munāfiqūn. The Level 1 description is: speakers of belief who are declared not believers.
2:2–5 — the Book and the muttaqūn (successful guided ones).
2:6–7 — those who have disbelieved (kafarū): warning is futile; God has sealed heart and hearing; a covering is on sight; great punishment.
2:8–16 — a third type: verbal believers who are not believers; disease; corruption claimed as reform; mockery; purchase of error for guidance.
2:17–20 — two similes (mathal): fire kindled then extinguished by God; rainstorm with darkness, thunder, lightning; they plug their ears; God is able over all things.

Person: God speaks as “We” in 2:3 (razaqnāhum) and is named Allah in 2:7, 2:8, 2:9, 2:10, 2:15, 2:19, 2:20. The addressee of 2:4 and 2:6 is singular “you” (ilayka / andhartahum). The Quran does not name that “you” in this block. Tradition: Muhammad. Classification of the identification: STRONG CONTEXTUAL PATTERN across the corpus still to be tested; in this block it is an OPEN named identification even though the grammar is second-person singular prophetic address.

Three isolated letters. No sentence. The Quran never glosses them. Later explanations (divine names, abbreviations, challenge that the Book is made of ordinary letters, numerical miracles, “only God knows”) are Level 4–5. DIRECT: the surah opens with these letters. OPEN: their intended meaning.
2:2  dhālika l-kitābu lā rayba fīhi hudan li-l-muttaqīn

“That/This is the Book: no rayb in it; guidance for the muttaqūn.” Dhālika is a distal demonstrative (“that”); many translators render “this.” Kitāb: writing/scripture/book. Rayb: doubt, suspicion, unease. The phrase does not say “the text will never have scribal variants” or “the Bible is corrupt.” It claims this kitāb is without rayb and is guidance for a class of people. Muttaqūn: those who practice taqwā (wary-guarding / God-consciousness / fear of God). Guidance is here restricted to that class, not said to be unusable by everyone. DIRECT: the Book is presented as undoubted guidance for the muttaqūn.
2:3  alladhīna yuʾminūna bi-l-ghaybi wa-yuqīmūna l-ṣalāta wa-mimmā razaqnāhum yunfiqūn

Three marks: they believe in the ghayb (unseen/absent); they establish the ṣalāh; they spend from what We provided. Ghayb is whatever is not present to ordinary perception; the verse does not list its contents. Ṣalāh here is the prayer (already a known ritual term in Arabic/Quranic usage; later fiqh specifies units). Infaq is spending/disbursing, not yet named zakāt. Divine “We” as provider. DIRECT: faith in unseen + ritual prayer + spending from provision.
2:4  wa-lladhīna yuʾminūna bi-mā unzila ilayka wa-mā unzila min qablika wa-bi-l-ākhirati hum yūqinūn

They believe in what was sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and they are certain of the ākhirah (hereafter/last). Unzila (passive): sent down. The verse affirms prior sent-down revelation as an object of belief for the successful, alongside the revelation to the addressee. It does not name Torah, Gospel, or Psalms here and does not say those earlier writings are textually intact or corrupt. DIRECT: dual belief in present and prior “sent-down” plus certainty of the hereafter. This is the project’s first Level 1 datum for QRQ-0003 and QRQ-0010.
2:5  ulāʾika ʿalā hudan min rabbihim wa-ulāʾika humu l-mufliḥūn
Those are upon guidance from their rabb; those are the successful (mufliḥūn). Closes the positive portrait. Connects to S001’s request for guidance and rabb.
2:6–7  inna lladhīna kafarū… khatama llāhu ʿalā qulūbihim…

Those who have disbelieved (kafarū): whether you warn them or not, they will not believe. Allah has sealed (khatama) their hearts and their hearing; over their sight is a covering (ghishāwah); for them is a great punishment (ʿadhāb ʿaẓīm).

Kafara’s root includes covering/concealing as well as ingratitude and rejection. The verse describes a class for whom warning does not produce faith. 2:7 attributes the seal to Allah. Classical tafsir commonly reads this as judicial consequence after persistent refusal, not arbitrary first causation (Level 4). The Arabic of 2:6–7 states the seal as God’s act and the unbelief as given. How that relates to human responsibility in 2:8–10 (they lie, they have disease, God increases the disease) is the first internal-agency tension of the project (QI-0001). DIRECT: God seals; warning does not avail this class; punishment is announced.

Some of the people say “We believe in Allah and the Last Day” but they are not believers. They try to deceive Allah and those who believe; they deceive only themselves and do not perceive. In their hearts is disease (maraḍ); God increases them in disease; painful punishment because they used to lie (yakdhibūn).

Level 1: verbal confession is distinguished from actual īmān. Deception language is used even of an attempt vis-à-vis God. Heart-disease + divine increase. Lying is the cited ground of punishment. Tradition: Medinan hypocrites around ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy (SIRAH/TAFSIR). Not in the verse.

When told not to corrupt (tufsidū) in the land, they say “we are only putters-right (muṣliḥūn).” The text retorts that they are the corrupters (mufsidūn) and do not perceive. When told “believe as the people believe,” they say “shall we believe as the fools (sufahāʾ) believe?” The text: they are the fools and do not know. When they meet the believers they say “we believe”; when alone with their shayāṭīn they say “we are with you; we were only mocking.” Allah mocks them and extends them in their ṭughyān (excess) while they wander blind. They bought error (ḍalālah) for guidance (hudā); their transaction did not profit; they were not guided.

DIRECT: double speech; reform-claim vs corruption-verdict; mockery; God as subject of mockery (yastahziʾu); exchange of guidance for error. Shayāṭīn here are their private counterparts — later theology may read demons or human ringleaders; the word is “their satans.” OPEN: exact referent of shayāṭīnihim in this verse.

Mathal of one who kindled a fire; when it lit what was around him, God took their light and left them in darkness, not seeing; deaf, dumb, blind; they do not return. Or like a rainstorm from the sky with darknesses, thunder, lightning; they put fingers in ears from the thunderbolts, fearing death; God encompasses the disbelievers. Lightning almost snatches their sight; whenever it lights for them they walk in it; when it darkens they halt; if God willed He would take their hearing and sight; God is over all things powerful (qadīr).

DIRECT: two extended similes of brief light then dark; divine power over hearing/sight; fear of death. The text does not decode the fire or the rain. Tafsir typically: hypocrites catch a little light of Islam then lose it; or the storm is the Quran itself. That decoding is Level 4.
Distal “that Book”; translators often “this.” Not a doctrinal split.
No doubt/suspicion in it — claim about the Book’s status as guidance, not a stemmatic statement.
Active participle of ittaqā: those who guard themselves (toward God).
Passive “sent down”; prior revelation is an object of required belief here.
God is the explicit subject of sealing hearts/hearing.
Covering over sight, paired with seal on heart/hearing.
Emphatic negation of their being believers despite the creed-sentence they utter.
“Their satans” — possessive; human or unseen referents both proposed later.
God as subject of mockery — anthropopathic verb; later theology will qualify.
Alif Lam Mim / A.L.M. — all leave untranslated
Correct. No English gloss is Level 1.
Kitāb can bear both; “Scripture” flags sacred writing.
conscious of Allah / mindful of God / ward off evil / fear Allah / godfearing
Taqwā is wariness + piety; “fear” alone is narrow; “mindful” is softer than the root.
Keep unseen; do not smuggle a later list (angels, God, last day) into 2:3 as if stated.
SI/Haleem/YA insert Muhammad or Prophet in brackets
Brackets are translator inference. Arabic is “to you.”
Core five generally do not insert “hypocrites” into 8–16 translation lines (notes do)
Good. The Arabic label is absent here.
Literal is satans/devils; “evil ones” is softening.

The Book claims unique epistemic status (no rayb) and restricted efficacy (guidance for muttaqūn). Believing success combines unseen-faith, prayer, spending, acceptance of present and prior revelation, and hereafter-certainty. Disbelief can be described as a state God seals. A third type can recite a correct-sounding creed and still be declared non-believers. God is provider (We), sealer, increaser of disease, mocker of mockers, and omnipotent over sense faculties. Punishment is announced before any legal code in this surah.
S001 asked for guidance on a path. S002 CP01 answers: guidance is this Book, for the muttaqūn, and some people will not take it.

Backward: S001 ṣirāṭ / hudā / rabb / dīn-as-judgment now meet kitāb, ghayb, ākhirah, ʿadhāb. Forward (not yet read in-project): sealing language (e.g. 4:155; 7:101; 10:74; 16:108; 45:23); munāfiqūn named (e.g. 4:88; 9:64–68; 63); confirmation of prior kitāb (2:41ff; 3:3; 5:44–48). QI-0001 (seal vs responsibility) must be reopened when later “they sealed themselves / God sealed because they disbelieved” verses are read.

Isaiah 6:9–10 and NT citations (Matt 13:14–15; John 12:40; Acts 28:26–27): God dulls/hardens perception of those who will not hear. Functional parallel to 2:6–7, not a quotation. Exodus / Romans hardening of Pharaoh is a related biblical motif still ahead of Quranic Pharaoh material.
Belief in prior scripture (2:4) overlaps formally with the Bible’s claim to be prior revelation, but 2:4 does not identify which books or their present textual state.
Psalm / wisdom “fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge” is a loose analogue to taqwā as the condition of guidance — thematic only.

PARTIAL AGREEMENT: God may judicially confirm people in blindness they have chosen (Isaiah/NT hardening // 2:7), pending later Quranic nuancing. PARTIAL AGREEMENT: prior revelation is real and to be believed (2:4) — without yet saying “the Bible in your hand is intact” or “the Bible in your hand is corrupt.” ADDITION vs typical biblical opening: isolated letters; three-type taxonomy including a verbal-believer who is not a believer. DIRECT CONTRADICTION: none declared in this block. See QB-0002, QB-0003.

Traditional setting: Medina after Hijrah, with open rejecters and a party that outwardly aligned with the Muslims. Sirah names ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy. That reconstruction explains why a third type appears here and not in S001, but it is SIRAH/TAFSIR, not stated by 2:8–20. Historically the phenomenon of partial or political conversion in a new prophetic polity is plausible. Certainty of the named identifications: traditional.

No biblical narrative retold. Parables of light/storm resemble sapiential and gospel simile technique (lamps, storms, blindness) without a specific source text demonstrated. Similarity ≠ dependency (Constitution §XVI).
Seals senses; increases disease; mocks mockers; provides; is qadīr over all things; speaks as We and as Allah.
First Level 1: successful people believe what was sent down before the addressee. No corruption claim here. No book titles.
Second-person singular addressee of revelation and warning. Name absent. Tradition supplies Muhammad.
Unzila “sent down” to you and before you. Kitāb with no rayb. Mechanism (angel, heart, language) not described here.
Success = guidance from rabb for muttaqūn defined in 2:3–4. Verbal creed insufficient (2:8).
Lying, disease of heart, corruption, mockery, purchase of error. No inherited Adamic guilt here.
Ākhirah certainty required; ʿadhāb ʿaẓīm / alīm announced; scenes not described.
Prior sent-down revelation is to be believed with the present sending-down. Relation is not yet named confirm / replace / correct.
2:1 isolated letters have no Quranic gloss
2:2 the Book is without rayb and is guidance for muttaqūn
2:3–5 believer marks: ghayb, salat, infaq, prior+present revelation, akhirah → success
2:4 requires belief in what was sent down before the addressee
2:6–7 warning-futile class; Allah seals heart/hearing; covering on sight
2:8–16 verbal believers declared non-believers; double speech; God mocks
2:17–20 fire and storm parables of brief light then dark
DIRECT as mathal; decoded referents OPEN
Sealed/hardened perception: 2:6–7 and Isaiah 6 / NT citations
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on judicial hardening motif; agency details OPEN (QI-0001)
2:4 belief in prior sent-down revelation vs biblical self-claim
PARTIAL AGREEMENT that prior revelation exists and matters; no textual-corruption or textual-integrity claim in 2:4
APPARENT TENSION — not yet a declared internal contradiction. Later seal-verses required.
“The Quran says it contains no doubt / has never changed.”
2:2 says no rayb in the kitāb as guidance. That is not a claim about manuscript history or qira'at. Overstatement if used as a textual-criticism shutdown.
2:4 affirms belief in what was sent down before the addressee. Titles, present text, and tahrif are not in this block. Claim is partly supported, incomplete.
Still no naming. 2:6–20 also names no community. Carry forward.

New or thickened lemmas in Registers: kitab, rayb, taqwa/muttaqin, ghayb, salat, infaq, nazzala/unzila, akhirah, yuqin, aflaha, kafara, khatama, qalb, ghishawah, adhab, amar, marad, fasad/islah, shaytan, tughyan, dalalah, mathal, qadir. See Dictionary sheet.
God: sealing, increasing disease, mocking, encompassing, qadir; speaks as We and Allah. Muhammad dossier opened as “unnamed second-person addressee of unzila and warning.” Jesus: no finding.
TAFSIR / SIRAH / STRONG later Quranic pattern — not named here
Seal as consequence not first cause

No testable geographic or datable public event is asserted in 2:1–20. Existence of a Medinan faction with dual speech is historically plausible and is the unanimous Islamic memory; extra-Islamic 7th-century documentation of that named faction is not established in this checkpoint. Classification: plausible, traditionally specified, extra-textually unverified.

2:1–20 opens the longest surah by placing a Book without rayb before three human types: the muttaqūn who combine unseen-faith, prayer, spending, present-and-prior revelation, and hereafter-certainty; the disbelievers whom warning will not move and whom God has sealed; and people who say the right creed but are not believers, whom God increases in disease and mocks.
