Prior revelation is an object of belief. Neither tahrif nor gospel/torah titles appear yet. Agency of seal versus human lying is logged as QI-0001, not resolved.
• Which prior “sent-down” writings, and in what state.
Next cut: 2:21–39 (worship-creation address through Adam/Iblis) unless a tighter rhetorical stop is used at 2:29.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP02 vv021-039
paragraphs: Cut rationale: New address at 2:21 (“O mankind”). Adam/Iblis unit closes at 2:39; 2:40 opens “O Children of Israel.”
Chronology tag: Medinan surah; this block not internally dated. Traditional.

After the three-type prologue (2:1–20), the text turns to all people: worship the creating Lord; do not set up andād (peers) for God; if you doubt what We sent down on Our servant, produce a surah like it — you never will — then fear the Fire whose fuel is people and stones. Believers who do righteous deeds are promised gardens. A gnat-parable follows: God guides and misleads by it. Then cosmology (life-death-life; earth then seven heavens) and the first long narrative: God announces a khalīfah on earth; angels object about corruption and bloodshed; Adam is taught the names; angels are commanded to prostrate; Iblīs refuses; Adam and his spouse are placed in the garden with one tree forbidden; Satan makes them slip; Adam receives words and God relents; descent to earth; guidance will come — followers have no fear or grief, rejecters are Fire-people.
2:21–22  Address to al-nās: worship + creation + no andād.
2:25      Gardens for those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt.
2:26–27  Gnat mathal; God misleads/guides; covenant-breakers lose.
2:28–29  Life cycle; earth then seven heavens.
Addressee shifts: mankind (21), doubters of the sending-down (23), “give good tidings” singular (25), “how do you disbelieve” (28), “your Lord said” to the Prophet-addressee (30).

Yā ayyuhā l-nāsu uʿbudū rabbakum: O people, worship your rabb who created you and those before you, so that you may practice taqwā. He made earth a firāsh (spread/couch) and sky a bināʾ (structure/canopy), sent water from the sky, brought forth fruits as rizq. So do not set up andād for God while you know.
DIRECT: worship grounded in creation and provision; peers/rivals forbidden. “While you know” implies some knowledge already possessed. Andād are equals/counterparts, not named here as specific idols.

If you are in rayb about what We sent down on Our servant (ʿabdinā), bring a sūrah min mithlihi and call your witnesses besides God, if you are truthful. If you do not — and you will never do it (wa-lan tafʿalū) — then guard against the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the kāfirīn.

DIRECT: the sending-down on “Our servant” is the object of possible doubt; a like-surah is demanded; inability is predicted as future-never (lan); Fire is prepared, fuel nās and ḥijārah. The servant is unnamed. Stones: later readings include ordinary fuel-stones or stone idols (cf. 21:98). Both are Level 4 options; Level 1 is “stones.” This is the project’s first iʿjāz/taḥaddī text. Other challenge verses (10:38; 11:13; 17:88; 52:33–34) are not yet read in-project.

Give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds: gardens under which rivers flow; whenever they are provided fruit they say “this is what we were provided before,” and they are given mutashābih (resembling) things; purified spouses; they abide.
DIRECT: faith + works together as the condition of the good news. Paradise is garden, rivers, fruit, spouses, permanence. Mutashābih here = resembling (the fruits), not the 3:7 technical term yet.

God does not shy from striking a mathal, even a gnat or above it. Those who believe know it is the truth from their Lord; the kāfirūn ask “what did God mean by this mathal?” He misleads (yuḍillu) many by it and guides (yahdī) many by it, and He misleads by it only the fāsiqīn — who break God’s covenant after its binding, cut what God ordered joined, and corrupt on earth; those are the losers.

DIRECT: God is subject of both iḍlāl and hidāyah. The misled class is identified as fāsiqīn with three behaviors. Which covenant is unnamed. This thickens QI-0001 rather than resolving it. A new QI is not required if QI-0001 is extended to 2:26; it is so extended.

How do you disbelieve in God? You were dead and He gave you life; then He will cause death, then life, then to Him you are returned. He created for you what is on the earth, then istawā toward the heaven and fashioned them seven heavens; He is knower of all things.

DIRECT: two deaths and two lives in sequence ending in return; seven heavens; God as ʿalīm. Istawā: settled/directed/then turned to. Later theology debates corporeality. Level 1: a verb of directed action toward heaven after earth-creation. Order stated: earth contents first, then heaven(s).

When your Lord said to the angels: I am placing in the earth a khalīfah. They said: will You place in it one who will corrupt and shed blood, while we hymn Your praise and sanctify You? He said: I know what you do not know. He taught Adam the names, all of them; presented them to the angels; “tell Me the names of these if you are truthful.” They: glory to You, no knowledge except what You taught us; You are the Knowing, the Wise. “O Adam, inform them of their names.” After he does: Did I not tell you I know the ghayb of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you disclose and what you were concealing?

DIRECT: planned earthly khalīfah; angels predict fasād and bloodshed; God claims superior knowledge including hidden things; Adam is taught all the names and can announce them; angels cannot. Khalīfah range: successor, deputy, vicegerent, succeeding generation. The verse does not say “deputy of God” in those words; jaʿil fī l-arḍi khalīfatan = placing a khalīfah in the earth. Whether Adam personally or humankind as succeeding occupants is debated in tafsir (Level 4). Names: the text says al-asmāʾa kullahā (“the names, all of them”) without listing referents.
When We said to the angels: prostrate to Adam, they prostrated except Iblīs; he refused, was proud, and was of the kāfirīn.

DIRECT: command to angels; universal compliance except Iblīs; refusal + pride; classification with those who reject. This block does not say Iblīs is a jinn (that is 18:50, not yet read). It also does not give the fire-versus-clay speech (7:12; 38:76). Those belong later. Sujūd toward Adam is commanded by God; later theology will distinguish worship of God from honor-prostration. Level 1: the command is usjudū li-ādama.

We said: O Adam, dwell you and your spouse (zawj) in the garden; eat freely but do not approach this tree lest you be of the ẓālimīn. But al-Shayṭān made them slip from it and expelled them from what they were in. We said: descend, some of you enemy to others; for you in the earth is settlement and enjoyment for a time.

DIRECT: unnamed spouse; unnamed tree; prohibition = “do not approach”; agent of the slip is al-Shayṭān (not here named Iblīs in 2:36, though 2:34 named Iblīs). Both are expelled; “some of you enemy to others” is plural. No snake. No order of who ate first. No “original guilt” language for descendants in this block — 2:38–39 will address descendants via guidance, not inherited stain.

Adam received (talaqqā) from his Lord words (kalimāt), and He relented toward him (tāba ʿalayhi); He is the Relenting, the Merciful. We said: descend from it all; when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance: no fear on them nor shall they grieve. Those who disbelieve and deny Our signs: those are companions of the Fire; they abide.

DIRECT: Adam is given words and receives tawbah from God. The words are not quoted here (7:23 will later supply a prayer; do not import it yet as if 2:37 cited it). Guidance from God is the ongoing term of earthly life. Followers: no khawf, no ḥuzn. Rejecters who also deny signs: Fire, abiding. Faith-plus-following vs kufr-plus-denial.
peers / counterparts set up for God (2:22)
a surah of/from its like — pronoun target debated: the sending-down or the servant
successor / deputy / succeeding occupant — not glossed
the names, all of them — referents unspecified
He turned in relenting upon him
become righteous / ward off evil / learn righteousness
laʿallakum tattaqūn — so you may practice taqwā
like it / like thereof / of its like
directed Himself / turned He / then rose / (Haleem often softens)
Do not let a theological school erase the verb.
Keep the Arabic term in analysis.
Unnamed; later Eve is tradition +  other passages’ pairing, not this verse’s name.
Most keep Satan here, Iblis in 34

God is creator of humankind and cosmos, forbids rivals, sends down speech on a servant, challenges doubters, prepares Fire and gardens, guides and misleads, knows the hidden, places a khalīfah, teaches Adam, commands angelic prostration, relents toward Adam after a slip caused by al-Shayṭān, and conditions earthly safety on following incoming guidance.

Humanity: created, provided for, capable of fasād and bloodshed (angels’ forecast), taught names, paired in the garden, slip-capable, able to receive words and tawbah, then placed on earth under a guidance alternative.

Salvation in this block: follow God’s incoming hudā → no fear/grief; believe + do ṣāliḥāt → gardens. No atonement-by-blood. Adam’s slip is met with given words and divine tawbah, not a curse on the race in these verses.
Iblīs: refuses, proud, of the kāfirīn. Relationship Iblīs = al-Shayṭān is the natural reading of 34–36 but is a synthesis until later identifying verses are read.

Backward: taqwā (2:2), rayb (2:2), ghayb (2:3), fasād (2:11–12), Fire (2:24 developing 2:7, 2:10). Forward: other Adam units (7:11–27; 15:28–44; 17:61–65; 18:50; 20:115–123; 38:71–85); other taḥaddī verses; 3:7 mutashābih (different use); Children of Israel begin 2:40.
QI-0001 extended to 2:26 (God misleads the fāsiqīn).
Genesis 1–3 is the controlling parallel: creation, human placement, garden, forbidden tree, tempter, expulsion, ongoing life east of the garden.
Present in both in some form: God as creator; a first human pair; a prohibited tree; a tempter; expulsion to a harder earthly life.

Absent from 2:21–39 vs Genesis: six-day structure; “image of God”; naming of animals by the man as dominion act in Gen 2; the woman as bone-of-bone with a personal name Ḥawwāh; the serpent; she-eats-first sequence; curses on serpent, woman, ground; cherubim and flaming sword; “knowledge of good and evil” as the tree’s name.

Present in 2:21–39 vs Genesis: angelic objection; khalīfah announcement; teaching of “all the names” as a knowledge test against angels; command that angels prostrate to Adam; Iblīs as proud refuse-r classed with kāfirīn; Adam receives words and God relents; explicit two-path sequel (follow guidance / deny signs).
PARTIAL AGREEMENT: a primordial pair in a garden, one forbidden tree, a tempter, expulsion to earth.

REINTERPRETATION: the meaning of the fall. Genesis frames disobedience + curse + toil + death’s entrance. 2:37–39 frames slip + received words + divine relenting + earthly life under forthcoming guidance, with Fire only for later kufr and denial of signs.
ADDITION (Quran): khalīfah council; names-test; angelic sujūd; Iblīs episode; taḥaddī; seven heavens in this placement.
OMISSION (vs Genesis): image of God; Eve’s name and birth from the side; serpent; ordered eating; specific curses.

DIRECT CONTRADICTION: not declared yet. The two accounts are not the same story with one detail flipped; they are overlapping origin narratives with different theological payloads. Contradiction protocol remains available if a later verse asserts a detail that cannot coexist with Genesis (e.g., explicit denial that a serpent was involved — not said here). See QB-0004, QB-0005.

Late antique Arabia knew biblical and para-biblical Adam material (Genesis, Life of Adam and Eve, cave-of-treasures type traditions, Syriac homily). Similarity is expected; dependency is not demonstrated by similarity alone (§XVI). The taḥaddī fits a setting where the “sending-down on Our servant” is publicly contested. Named historical persons other than Adam/Iblīs: none.

Genesis 1–3; possible late-antique expansions where Satan refuses to honor Adam (found in some Jewish and Christian extra-canonical tellings). Status: similarity / possible relationship. Not logged as demonstrable literary dependency in this checkpoint.
Creator, forbids andād, sends down, challenges, prepares Fire/gardens, guides and misleads, ʿalīm of ghayb, relents (tawwāb).
No book titles. “Signs” (āyāt) denied by the Fire-bound (2:39).
ʿAbdinā and “give tidings” and “your Lord said” continue the unnamed servant/addressee.
Tanzīl on the servant; taḥaddī as authentication test; lan tafʿalū as predicted inimitability.
Believe + ṣāliḥāt → gardens. Follow incoming hudā → no fear/grief. Tawbah available to Adam after words given.
Slip of the pair via Shayṭān; they become ẓālimīn if they approach the tree; no inherited-guilt sentence in 2:37–39.
Fire (people+stones fuel) prepared; gardens with rivers, fruit, spouses, abiding; return to God after second life.
Not a continuity-with-Bible thesis statement. Narrative overlap with Genesis is real and theologically recast.
Worship grounded in creation; andād forbidden (2:21–22)
Taḥaddī: produce a surah like what was sent down on Our servant; you never will (2:23–24)
Faith plus righteous deeds promised gardens (2:25)
God guides and misleads by the mathal; only fāsiqīn are misled (2:26–27)
Khalīfah announcement; angels object; Adam taught all the names (2:30–33)
Angels prostrate to Adam; Iblīs refuses, proud, of the kāfirīn (2:34)
Garden, unnamed tree and spouse; Shayṭān causes both to slip; descent (2:35–36)
Adam receives words; God relents; earthly two-path (guidance vs Fire) (2:37–39)
PARTIAL AGREEMENT + REINTERPRETATION + ADDITION + OMISSION. No Direct Contradiction declared.
Fall theology: inherited Adamic guilt vs slip + tawbah + later personal kufr
REINTERPRETATION. Genesis/Pauline original-sin systems are not the payload of 2:37–39. Later Quranic verses may thicken this.

QI-0001 extended to 2:26 (yuḍillu / yahdī). No new QI number. No internal contradiction declared between 2:21 “worship so that you may have taqwā” and 2:6 “they will not believe” — different addressees/classes can sit together as complementary. Status of that pairing: complementary pending later universal/particular verses.
“The Quran challenges anyone to produce a surah like it and this proves divine origin.”

2:23–24 is a real taḥaddī plus lan tafʿalū. Whether historical unmet-challenge equals metaphysical proof is a philosophical step beyond Level 1. Record the textual challenge as DIRECT; the evidential inference as SYNTHESIS / contested.
2:37–39 gives Adam tawbah and places descendants under forthcoming guidance, not under a stated inherited guilt. Strong textual pattern beginning, not yet a full-corpus doctrine declaration.

New lemmas: andad, abd, surah, tahaddi/mithl, hijarah, jannat, salihat, fasaqa, ahd, istawa, sab' samawat, khalifah, asma, malak, sajada, Iblis, zawj, shajarah, zall/azalla, talaqqa, kalimah, taba/tawwab, khawf, huzn, aya.

God updated. Adam dossier opened. Muhammad dossier: ʿabdinā + prophetic “your Lord said.” Jesus: no finding. Iblīs logged inside Adam dossier and Dictionary pending a dedicated figure file if later volume warrants — Constitution allows figures inside existing dossier architecture.
JEWISH TRADITION + later Islamic naming; not in 2:35

Adam narrative is not archaeologically testable as a dated event. Seven-heavens cosmology matches widespread late-antique Near Eastern models; that is cultural consistency, not verification of the cosmology. Taḥaddī is a literary-historical claim about inimitability; evaluating later Arabic production against it is a separate scholarly debate, not settled here. Classification: historically untestable origin narrative + culturally situated cosmology + textual challenge.

2:21–39 moves from a universal worship-command and an inimitability challenge to the first major origin story. God places a khalīfah; teaches Adam names the angels do not know; commands prostration; Iblīs refuses in pride; the pair slip by Satan and descend; Adam is given words and God relents; earth becomes a timed dwelling under forthcoming guidance. Gardens attach to faith-plus-deeds; Fire to kufr-plus-denial. The Genesis overlap is real; the theology of the slip is not Pauline original sin in this block.
• Referent of mithlihi and historical status of the taḥaddī.
• Sense of khalīfah; contents of “all the names.”
Next: S002 CP03 from 2:40 (Children of Israel address). Proposed close ~2:61 or 2:66 depending on rhetorical volume.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP03 vv040-061
paragraphs: Why this cut: Opens Banū Isrāʾīl address; first Exodus cycle closes at 2:61. 2:62 starts a new sentence on Jews/Christians/Sabians.
Comparison priority: Owner request: run Bible comparison wherever the narratives actually meet. This block meets Exodus–Numbers and judgment/intercession texts.

God addresses the Children of Israel in the second person as if the Medinan audience stands in continuity with the Exodus generation: remember My favor; fulfill My covenant; believe in what I sent down confirming what is with you; do not conceal truth; establish prayer and give zakāt. Then a Day is announced on which no soul avails another, no intercession is accepted, no ransom taken, no help given. A rapid Exodus recitation follows: Pharaoh’s torment, sea-parting, forty nights, the calf, Moses’ book and furqān, “kill yourselves,” demand to see God and a death-revival, cloud / manna / salwā, a town-entry word they changed, twelve springs from a struck stone, complaint about one food, “go down to Egypt,” humiliation and wrath because they disbelieved signs and killed the prophets.
2:40–46  Covenant call + present duties (believe the confirming sending-down; prayer; zakāt; patience).
2:47–48  Favor/preference + Day with no substitution, shafāʿah, ʿadl (ransom), or help.
2:49–61  Favors-and-failures catalogue (Exodus cycle), ending in a verdict: humiliation, wrath, prophet-killing.
The “you” is plural Children of Israel, including the living addressees. That rhetorical collapse of generations is a Quranic device, not a claim that the Medinan Jews personally crossed the sea.
3. Verse Investigation (clustered where formulaic; line-level at comparison points)

O Children of Israel: remember My niʿmah; fulfill My ʿahd and I will fulfill yours; fear Me. Believe in what I sent down, muṣaddiqan li-mā maʿakum (confirming what is with you); do not be the first to disbelieve in it; do not sell My signs for a small price; fear Me. Do not mix the truth with falsehood or conceal the truth while you know. Establish ṣalāh, give zakāt, bow with those who bow. Do you command birr and forget yourselves while you recite the Book? Seek help in ṣabr and ṣalāh; it is hard except for the khāshiʿīn who think they will meet their Lord and return to Him.

DIRECT (QRQ-0003 / 0010): the new sending-down is described as confirming what Israel already has with them. That is stronger than 2:4’s generic “what was sent before you.” It still does not name the Torah, describe its present wording as intact, or charge textual corruption. Concealment (taktumū) and mixing truth with falsehood are about handling known truth, which may be oral, written, or interpretive — the verse does not specify manuscript alteration.
Zakāt appears here as a command to this audience (first explicit pairing with ṣalāh in our reading).
2:47–48  Preference and a Day without substitution

Remember the favor and that I preferred you over the ʿālamīn. Fear a Day when no nafs will suffice for another at all; no shafāʿah accepted from it; no ʿadl (equivalent/ransom) taken; they will not be helped.

DIRECT: eschatological individualization. Preference “over the worlds” is a historical-election claim about Israel (cf. 2:122 later). 2:48 is the project’s first Level 1 intercession text, and it is negative. Later verses that allow intercession by permission (e.g. 2:255; 20:109 — not yet read) must be logged against this as possible QI, not silently harmonized now. Christian comparison: substitutionary help / intercession of Christ is a different architecture. Jewish comparison: Ezekiel 18 individual responsibility overlaps; temple/atonement systems are another register. See QB-0006.

We saved you from Pharaoh’s folk who afflicted you with evil torment, slaying sons and sparing women — a great trial from your Lord. We parted the sea, saved you, drowned Pharaoh’s folk while you looked on.

AGREEMENT with Exodus 1 and 14–15 on the core plot: oppression, male-child policy, sea opening, drowning of the pursuers. ADDITION/OMISSION vs Exodus: no named Moses yet in 49–50 (he enters at 51); no staff-stretching detail here; Pharaoh’s person is “his folk” drowned in view — Exodus 14:28 drowns the army and is debated on Pharaoh himself. No Song of the Sea. See QB-0007.

We appointed Moses forty nights; then you took the calf after him, while wrongdoers. Then We pardoned you. We gave Moses the kitāb and the furqān so you might be guided. Moses: you have wronged yourselves by taking the calf; repent to your bāriʾ and kill yourselves (fa-qtulū anfusakum); that is better for you with your Maker. Then He relented toward you; He is al-Tawwāb al-Raḥīm.

AGREEMENT: Moses away forty days/nights (Exodus 24:18; 34:28); calf in his absence (Exodus 32); a written revelation associated with that meeting; a lethal consequence among the people; subsequent mercy.

DIFFERENCE: Exodus 32:26–29 — Levites kill about three thousand of the people at Moses’ command from YHWH. 2:54 — Moses tells the people to repent and “kill yourselves.” Anfusakum can mean your own selves or some among you (the calf-party). Haleem-style glosses insert “[the guilty among] you.” That is interpretation. Level 1 is the phrase as written. Aaron’s role in making the calf is absent here (present in Exodus 32; Quran 20:90–94 later). The Samaritan figure of 20:85 is absent here.
Furqān: criterion/divider/salvation — not a second book title forced by grammar.
2:55–57  “We will not believe until we see God”; cloud, manna, salwā

You said: we will not believe you until we see God openly (jahratan). The ṣāʿiqah seized you while you looked on. Then We raised you after your death so you might be grateful. We shaded you with cloud and sent down al-mann and al-salwā: eat of the good things. They did not wrong Us; they wronged themselves.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT: Israel’s fear/demand around seeing God at the mountain (Exodus 19–20; Deut 4–5); manna and quail (Exodus 16; Numbers 11); cloud cover (Exodus 13:21–22; Psalm 105:39).

DIFFERENCE: Exodus does not narrate the people struck dead for saying “we will not believe until we see God” and then bodily revived as a group. The Quranic ṣāʿiqah + death + revival is an ADDITION relative to the canonical Exodus scene (which has terror, trumpet, threat of death if they break through, but not this revival). See QB-0008.
2:58–59  Enter the town; ḥiṭṭah; they changed the word

We said: enter this qaryah; eat freely; enter the gate sajadan and say ḥiṭṭah (unburdening/forgiveness); We will forgive. The wrongdoers substituted a saying other than what was said to them; We sent down rijz from the sky on the wrongdoers for their fisq.

Town unnamed (tafsir: Jericho or a Jerusalem gate — Level 4). Ḥiṭṭah has no exact biblical password-at-the-gate parallel in Joshua 6 or Deuteronomy. Closest biblical analogue is entering the land under command, plus later prophetic charges that Israel twisted words (Jeremiah 8:8 is a different charge). Hadith supplies a mocking substitute word — HADITH, not 2:59. Level 1: they replaced the commanded saying; a sky-punishment followed. See QB-0009.

When Moses sought drink for his people, We said: strike the stone with your staff. Twelve springs burst; each people knew its drinking-place. Eat and drink of God’s rizq; do not act wickedly corrupting the earth.

PARTIAL AGREEMENT: water from a rock struck by Moses’ staff (Exodus 17:1–7; Numbers 20:2–13). ADDITION: twelve springs mapped to groups (Elim in Exodus 15:27 has twelve springs and seventy palms, but that is an oasis, not a struck rock). Quranic fusion of rock-miracle + twelve-tribe watering is a distinct configuration. Numbers 20’s striking-in-anger / exclusion from Canaan is absent here.
2:61  One food; Egypt; humiliation; killed the prophets

You said: we will not endure one food; ask your Lord for herbs, cucumbers, garlic, lentils, onions. He: would you exchange what is better for what is lower? Go down to a miṣr (settlement/Egypt); you will have what you asked. Humiliation and poverty were struck upon them; they returned with wrath from God — because they disbelieved God’s signs and killed the prophets without right, because they disobeyed and used to transgress.
AGREEMENT with Numbers 11:4–6 on the food complaint (manna vs fish/cucumbers/melons/leeks/onions/garlic of Egypt) and the theme of preferring Egypt’s menu.

DIFFERENCE: Numbers 11 answers with quail and a plague, not “go down to Egypt / a city.” Miṣr can mean Egypt or a town. “Killed the prophets without right” is a verdict spanning more than the wilderness generation (biblical narrative of prophet-killing is mostly later: e.g. 1 Kings 19:10; 2 Chron 24:20–22; Neh 9:26; Matt 23:29–37; Luke 11:47–51; Acts 7:52). Using it as the ground of 2:61’s humiliation compresses many centuries into one “you.” See QB-0010, QB-0011.
confirming that which is with you — present possession, not “which used to be with your ancestors only”
conceal the truth — act, not a named textual edition
kill yourselves / kill your own (people) — ambiguity is real
they kill the prophets without right
confirming what is with you — stable across core five
Do not translate as “the Bible is uncorrupted” or “the Bible is corrupted.”
Do not insert “except by God’s leave” here; that is other verses.
kill yourselves / slay the guilty among you (Haleem-type)

Israel is addressed as covenant partner who already possesses earlier revelation that the new sending-down confirms. Handling that possession wrongly (concealment, mixing, cheap sale of signs) is sin. Election (“preferred over the worlds”) coexists with a Day of non-transferable liability. Mercy after the calf coexists with a lethal repentance command. Wilderness gifts (cloud, manna, quail, water) are remembered as favors they answered with complaint and later with prophet-killing. God remains tawwāb after the calf as after Adam.

Backward: 2:4 prior tanzīl; 2:27 broken covenant; Adam tawbah. Forward: 2:62 (next packet); 2:87, 91 prophet-killing reprises; 2:123 near-repeat of 2:48; 7:103–162 parallel Exodus cycle; 20 calf/Sāmirī; 4:153–155; intercession-permission verses to test against 2:48.
8–9. Biblical Cross-References and Agreement / Difference (combined by episode)
This is the comparison core of the packet. Classifications follow Constitution §VII. A difference is not automatically a contradiction.
No one avails another; no accepted intercession/ransom
Ezek 18; Deut 24:16; Ps 49:7–9; vs also Isa 53 / NT priestly intercession
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with individual-responsibility texts. REINTERPRETATION vs substitutionary atonement systems. Later Quranic shafāʿah-by-permission not yet in play.
AGREEMENT on plot. OMISSION of named Moses here, staff gesture, Song of the Sea. Pharaoh-person drowning OPEN vs Exod 14:28.
Forty nights, calf, seeing God, manna/quail/cloud
AGREEMENT on absence, calf, mountain terror, manna/quail/cloud. ADDITION: group death by ṣāʿiqah and revival. OMISSION: Aaron as calf-maker; tablets smashed; Levite slaughter detail.

PARTIAL AGREEMENT that the calf brought a killing command. DIFFERENCE in who kills whom. Not declared Direct Contradiction: both can describe a lethal purge; they do not tell the same operational story.
Enter town saying ḥiṭṭah; word substituted
No close Exodus/Joshua password parallel; Jer 8:8 is a different “lying pen” charge
ADDITION relative to the canonical Hexateuch scene. Possible midrashic/oral analogue remains OPEN (Narrative Tracker: possible relationship, not demonstrated dependency).
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on staff + rock water. ADDITION of twelve assigned springs at the struck stone. OMISSION of Meribah-anger / Moses barred from Canaan.
Food complaint; Egypt menu; prophet-killing verdict
Num 11:4–6; later 1 Kgs 19:10; Neh 9:26; Matt 23:37; Acts 7:52
AGREEMENT on the menu-complaint. REINTERPRETATION/ADDITION: humiliation grounded in kufr + killing prophets — a verdict that in the Bible is mostly later than the wilderness.
New sending-down confirms what is with you
Torah self-claim; NT “fulfill not abolish” (Matt 5:17) is a different axis
PARTIAL AGREEMENT that prior scripture is real and present. OPEN: whether “what is with you” means intact text, distorted reading, or both. Not yet tahrif.

Medinan address to a Jewish audience that the Quran treats as heirs of Israel’s covenant memory. That setting explains the second-person “you crossed the sea.” Historically, 7th-century Hijazi Jews possessed scripture and interpretive tradition; the exact codices in Yathrib are not recoverable from this block. Prophet-killing as a stock charge exists in biblical and extra-biblical Jewish and Christian memory before Islam.

Primary: Hebrew Bible Exodus–Numbers. Secondary: possible late antique homiletic expansions (twelve springs at the rock; death-and-revival at Sinai). Similarity logged; demonstrable written dependency not claimed.
Covenant partner; savior from Pharaoh; giver of kitāb/furqān; tawwāb after calf; strikes rijz; prefers Israel; judges a Day without transfer.
2:41 confirming what is with you; 2:42 conceal/mix; 2:44 you recite the Book. Strongest prior-scripture datum yet. No tahrif word.
Implied as bearer of the confirming sending-down; still unnamed.
Tanzīl that confirms prior possession; kitāb + furqān given to Moses.
2:48 blocks substitution/ransom/intercession in that sentence. Calf episode: tawbah + lethal command + divine relenting.
Concealment, mixing, calf, word-substitution, complaint, prophet-killing, fisq.
Day of no avail; Fire not restated; meeting the Lord (2:46).
Confirmation language (muṣaddiq). Not replacement language in this block.
2:40–46 Israel covenant; confirming what is with you; conceal not the truth
2:48 Day: no soul avails another; no accepted shafāʿah; no ransom; no help
DIRECT as Quranic recitation; comparison in QB-0007–0011
2:61 humiliation grounded in kufr of signs + killing prophets
QB-0006 through QB-0012 issued above. No Direct Contradiction declared. Several REINTERPRETATION and ADDITION calls.

QI-0002 opened: 2:48 universal-sounding refusal of intercession vs later Quranic texts that mention intercession by permission (to be filled when those verses are read). Status: apparent tension pending the later verses — not a contradiction yet because the later evidence is not in-project.
Strengthened by 2:41 muṣaddiqan li-mā maʿakum. Still no integrity certificate and no tahrif charge.
“The Quran says there is no intercession.”
2:48 says none accepted on that Day in that sentence. Overstated if treated as the Quran’s last word before later shafāʿah verses are read.

2:61 states they killed the prophets without right. That is a Quranic claim. Historical audit of each named biblical prophet’s death is a separate Historical Claim Audit — not all HB prophets are said in the HB to have been killed.
Isra'il, 'ahd, musaddiq, katama, zakat, shafa'ah, 'adl (ransom), Fir'awn, 'ijl, furqan, bari', sa'iqah, mann, salwa, hittah, baddala, 'asa, misr, nabiyy.
Moses dossier opened. God updated (election of Israel; tawwāb after calf; no-transfer Day). Muhammad still unnamed bearer of confirming tanzīl. Jesus none. Adam none new.

Exodus as a large-scale Late Bronze event remains historically disputed in modern scholarship; this project records that the Quran and the Bible share the tradition, not that archaeology has verified the numbers. “Killed the prophets”: some biblical prophets are murdered in HB narrative; many are not; NT generalizes the charge. Classification of 2:61 as history: disputed / tradition-level, not independently demonstrated for a complete list of prophets.

Israel is called to honor a covenant the new sending-down confirms. A Day is coming when no one stands in for anyone. The Exodus is retold as a favor they answered with the calf, a demand to see God, a changed word, and a craving for Egypt’s food — ending in humiliation because of kufr and prophet-killing. Where the Bible and Quran tell the same episodes, the plot often agrees and the operational details often do not (who kills after the calf; death-revival at the mountain; twelve springs at the rock; ḥiṭṭah). Confirmation of “what is with you” is now explicit. Tahrif is still not.
• What “what is with you” includes, physically.
Next proposed: S002 CP04 = 2:62–74 (or 2:62–82 if still manageable), beginning with Jews, Christians, and Sabians.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP04 vv062-082
paragraphs: Why this cut: 2:62 opens Jews/Christians/Sabians. 2:67–73 is the cow that names the surah. 2:75–79 is the first yuharrifūna / write-the-book block. 2:83 begins a new Israel pledge list.
Comparison priority: Salvation-scope (2:62); mountain covenant; Sabbath; cow // Num 19 and Deut 21; first explicit taḥrīf-adjacent verses.

This block does four jobs. (1) 2:62 states that believers, Jews, Christians, and Sabians — whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does ṣāliḥ — have their reward, no fear, no grief. (2) 2:63–66 return to Israel: mountain raised over them; they turned away; some Sabbath-breakers told “be despised apes.” (3) 2:67–74: Moses commands a cow-slaughter; they stall with questions (age, color ṣafrāʾ, unused, unblemished); they kill a person and dispute; God says strike the dead with part of the cow; God shows He raises the dead. (4) 2:75–82: do not expect them all to believe; a party used to hear kalām Allāh then distort it (yuḥarrifūnahu) after understanding it, knowingly; some are ummiyyūn who know the Book only as amānī; woe to those who write the kitāb with their hands then say “this is from God” for a small price; they say Fire will touch them only numbered days; the reply is: no such covenant, or you speak of God what you do not know. Evildoers engulfed by sin → Fire abiding; faith + ṣāliḥāt → Garden abiding.
72–74  unsolved killing + striking with a piece of the cow + resurrection sign.
75–79  distortion / illiteracy / writing a book and attributing it to God.
80–82  short-stay-in-Fire claim vs abiding Fire / Garden.
Inna lladhīna āmanū wa-lladhīna hādū wa-l-naṣārā wa-l-ṣābiʾīna man āmana bi-llāhi wa-l-yawmi l-ākhiri wa-ʿamila ṣāliḥan fa-lahum ajruhum ʿinda rabbihim wa-lā khawfun ʿalayhim wa-lā hum yaḥzanūn.

DIRECT: four named groups; the reward condition is belief in God + Last Day + righteous deed. Same “no fear / no grief” cadence as 2:38. The verse does not mention belief in Muhammad. SI and some tafsir insert “[before Muhammad]” or “true belief = Islam.” Those are Level 4/5 restrictions. Level 1 wording is the condition as stated. Sabians: identity disputed (star-worshippers, a Book-people, a group between religions). OPEN historically. This verse must be read later against 3:85 and 2:120 etc. Possible QI when those arrive. See QCA-0001 thickening and QB-0013.
Covenant taken; the mountain (al-ṭūr) raised above you; hold firmly what We gave you and remember what is in it. Then you turned away; but for grace and mercy you would have been losers.

PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Exodus 19: the mountain, covenant, “hold what was given.” ADDITION: the mountain lifted over them as a threat-sign (also 4:154; 7:171). Exodus has the mountain shaking and bounded; it does not say it was physically hoisted overhead. Later midrash sometimes dramatizes Sinai; dependency not demonstrated. See QB-0014.
You already knew those among you who transgressed the Sabbath; We said: be apes, despised. We made it a nakāl for those before and after, and an exhortation for the muttaqīn.

DIRECT: a Sabbath violation answered by a divine speech that makes them qirada. Whether literal metamorphosis or figurative humiliation is tafsir (Level 4). Biblical Sabbath-breaking (Num 15:32–36) is stoning of a wood-gatherer, not transformation into apes. This is ADDITION / REINTERPRETATION relative to the canonical HB episode. See QB-0015.

Moses: God commands you to slaughter a baqara. They: are you mocking us? He seeks refuge from being among the jāhilīn. They ask what it is → neither old nor young, in between. Color → ṣafrāʾ fāqiʿ, pleasing to beholders. What it is, cows look alike → not yoked to plow or water, sound, no shiya. They slaughter it, having almost not done so.

The passage reads as delay-by-question. It supplies the surah title. Biblical counterparts are two different rites: Numbers 19 red heifer (parah adummah, unblemished, never yoked, burned for ash-water) and Deuteronomy 21 heifer whose neck is broken in an unsolved homicide. Quranic color is ṣafrāʾ (usually yellow; range can include tawny). Saadia Gaon later rendered the biblical “red” with a cognate that can mean yellow — historical linguistics, not proof the Quran meant “red.” See QB-0016.
2:72–74  The killing and the piece of the cow

You killed a nafs and disputed about it; God is the one who brings out what you were concealing. We said: strike him with part of it. God brings the dead to life and shows you His signs. Then your hearts hardened after that, like stones or harder; some stones rivers burst from; some split and water comes; some fall from fear of God. God is not unaware of what you do.

The cow slaughter is here tied to revealing a murderer and to a resuscitation sign. Deut 21:1–9 uses an unused heifer in a valley to clear bloodguilt; it does not raise the victim. Numbers 19 purifies corpse-contact; it does not identify a killer. Quranic scene fuses cow-rite + homicide + revival. ADDITION relative to both biblical rites. Hearts-as-stones continues the seal/hardness theme (QI-0001 family).
Do you [Muslims] hope they will believe you, when a party of them used to hear the speech of God then distort it (yuḥarrifūnahu) after they had understood it, while they know?

DIRECT: a farīq (party), not “all Jews”; they heard kalām Allāh; they distort after ʿaql (understanding); they know they are doing it. The verb is the same root later discussed as taḥrīf. This verse does not say “they rewrote every copy of the Torah on earth.” It says a party distorted God’s speech after grasping it. Classical tafsir splits between altering meaning and altering words (description of Muhammad; legal rulings). Academic readers often stress displacement of words from their places (cf. 5:13 later). Level 1 here: knowing distortion of heard divine speech by a party. See QDISC-0028, QCA-0009, QB-0017.

When they meet those who believe they say “we believe”; when alone with each other they say: will you tell them what God opened to you so they may argue with you before your Lord? Do they not know God knows what they conceal and reveal? Among them are ummiyyūn who do not know the Book except amānī (wishes / recited fancies) and they only guess.

Double speech recalls 2:14. Ummiyyūn: commonly “unlettered,” here people who do not know the Book except wishes. Two populations among “them”: a party that heard and distorted (75), and illiterates who do not know the Book (78). That internal split matters: the Quran is not describing a single uniform Jewish relationship to scripture.
2:79  they write the kitāb with their hands
Woe to those who write the kitāb with their hands then say “this is from God,” to buy with it a small price. Woe for what their hands wrote and for what they earn.

DIRECT: some people produce writing, ascribe it to God, for gain. This is the strongest “false scripture production” sentence so far. It still does not say “the Torah in your hand is entirely this fabrication.” It condemns writers who attribute their product to God. Tafsir often specifies changed prophetic description. Reynolds-type reading: treating human words as revelation. Both go beyond the bare clause. Level 1 = writing + “this is from God” + small price. See QCA-0009.

They say the Fire will not touch us except days numbered. Say: have you taken a covenant from God — God does not break His covenant — or do you say of God what you do not know? Whoever earns evil and is surrounded by his sin → companions of the Fire, abiding. Those who believe and do ṣāliḥāt → companions of the Garden, abiding.

The “few days in Fire” claim is treated as unauthorized. Mishnah Eduyot 2:10 and related Jewish discussion of a twelve-month Gehinnom for some is a possible background (possible relationship, not proven quotation). Faith + deeds vs engulfing sin restates 2:25 / 2:39.
Jews (those who judaized), Nazarenes/Christians, Sabians — last OPEN
We raised the mountain above you
strike him with part of it (the cow)
they distort / displace it — after understanding, knowingly
they write the book with their hands
SI/Khattab often historicize “before Muhammad”; Haleem/Pickthall more open
Do not let a bracket become Level 1.
Arabic is apes; metaphor is tafsir.
Keep the verb; do not print “rewrote the Bible” as the translation.
Indefinite sense of produced writing is possible.

Reward language in 2:62 is conditioned on God, Last Day, and ṣāliḥ work, and names Jews and Christians inside that sentence. Israel remains under covenant memory (mountain) and under charges of Sabbath breach, stalling at a commanded slaughter, homicide concealment, knowing distortion of heard speech, and selling God-attribution. Fire-duration is not a human claim they get to set. Hearts can harden past stone. God raises the dead (cow-sign).
2:38 no fear/grief; 2:41 confirming what is with you; 2:48 intercession; 2:61 prophet-killing. Forward: 3:85; 5:13, 41 yuḥarrifūna l-kalima; 5:69 near-repeat of 2:62; 7:163–166 Sabbath apes; 4:46.
Acts 4:12; John 14:6; also Rom 2:6–16; Gentile-inclusion debates

PARTIAL AGREEMENT that God, last day, and deeds matter. Tension with exclusive NT “no one comes to the Father except through me” if 2:62 is read without later Islamic restriction. Not a Direct Contradiction until 3:85 and NT exclusivism are both in the register together.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT (covenant at the mountain). ADDITION: mountain raised above.
Num 19 red heifer; Deut 21 unsolved-murder heifer

PARTIAL AGREEMENT (unused, unblemished cow/heifer). ADDITION: yellow; questioning delay; strike corpse with a piece; victim revived. Color mismatch with MT “red” is real in ordinary translation; not yet declared Direct Contradiction because ṣafrāʾ’s range and later Judeo-Arabic rendering of adummah are live linguistic issues.
Distorting / writing as if from God
Jer 8:8 “lying pen of the scribes”; Deut 4:2; Rev 22:18–19 (do not add)

PARTIAL AGREEMENT that false ascription and twisting of divine words is condemned in both canons. The Quran here targets a party and writers-for-gain, not a completed scholarly proof that the entire Masoretic Text or NT is fabricated.

Medinan polemic with Jews who possess scripture. Sabians remain historically fuzzy. Sabbath-ape story has no extra-Quranic 7th-century Jewish source identified in this checkpoint. Cow narrative sits in a late-antique world that knew both Num 19 and Deut 21 and rabbinic specification-lists.
Num 19; Deut 21; possible midrashic Sinai-mountain imagery; possible Gehinnom-duration traditions behind 2:80. Similarity / possible relationship. Not demonstrable single-source copying.
Raises mountain; transforms Sabbath-breakers; raises dead; knows secret/open; does not break covenant.
Major: 2:75 party distorts heard speech; 2:78 some do not know the Book; 2:79 some write a book and say it is from God. Still not “the Bible as a whole is textually void.”
Implied addressee of 2:75 “do you hope they will believe you.”
Kalām Allāh can be heard and then distorted; false writing can be sold as divine.
2:62 reward formula; 2:81–82 Fire/Garden by engulfing evil vs iman+deeds. Numbered-days claim rejected.
Sabbath breach; stalling; homicide concealment; knowing distortion; writing-for-gain; speaking of God without knowledge.
Fire not limited to numbered days; Garden/Fire abiding.
2:62 names Jews and Christians inside a reward sentence. Confirmation-vs-distortion now sit in the same surah (2:41 and 2:75/79).
2:75 a party heard God's speech and distorted it after understanding, knowingly
2:78 some ummiyyun know the Book only as amani
2:79 woe to those who write the kitāb with their hands and say it is from God
2:80–82 numbered-days-in-Fire claim rejected; abiding Fire vs Garden

QI-0003 opened: 2:41 “confirming what is with you” vs 2:75/79 distortion/writing-as-divine. Not a contradiction yet: one can confirm a prior sending-down and still accuse a party of mishandling or fabricating. Status: apparent tension / complementary-possible. Do not collapse into “the Quran both affirms and denies the Bible” without finishing 4:46, 5:13–15, 5:43–47.
QI-0004 reserved for 2:62 vs later exclusivist verses (3:85 unread).
Same God / same salvation as Christianity
2:62 names Christians in a reward formula. Still OPEN as a full identity-of-conception claim.
“The Quran says the Bible was corrupted.”

2:75 and 2:79 are the first strong data. They condemn a party’s distortion of heard speech and writers who ascribe their product to God. They do not, by themselves, equal “every biblical manuscript is fabricated.” Claim as popularly stated is OVERBROAD for this block alone.
Still true via 2:41; now qualified by 2:75/79. Both must stay on the table.
Nasara, Sabi'un, Tur, qird, baqara, safra', harrafa, ummi, amani, wayl, ma'dud.
God: 2:62 reward; mountain; apes command; cow specs; raises dead; knows hidden. Moses: cow interrogation. Jesus: still unnamed; “Christians” as a community appear (al-naṣārā).
2:79 = they changed Muhammad’s description in the Torah

Sabian identity: insufficient evidence. Sabbath-ape incident: no extra-Quranic verification in this checkpoint. Cow-homicide revival: narrative, not archaeologically testable. 2:79 as a claim about specific Medinan copyists: plausible polemic setting, unverified as a described workshop.

2:62 puts Jews and Christians inside a God / Last Day / good-works reward sentence. The same stretch accuses a party of knowingly distorting heard divine speech and others of writing a book and calling it God’s for a price. The cow story that names the surah sits between Numbers 19 and Deuteronomy 21 without being identical to either (yellow; delay; piece of the cow raises the murdered man). 2:41 and 2:75/79 now have to be carried together: confirmation of what is with them, and a charge of distortion and false ascription by some.
• 2:62 vs later exclusivism (QI-0004 when 3:85 is read).
• Exact scope of taḥrīf (words vs meaning vs whole canon).
• Next: S002 CP05 from 2:83 (Israel pledge, killing, expulsion, “We gave Moses the Book / We sent messengers / Jesus son of Mary with clear signs”). Jesus dossier will finally receive Quranic lines.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP05 vv083-101
paragraphs: Why this cut: New mīthāq list at 2:83. First sequential naming of Jesus at 2:87. 2:102 Harut/Marut is a different dossier (magic) — next packet.

God reminds a covenant with Israel: worship God alone; iḥsān to parents, kin, orphans, poor; speak ḥusn to people; prayer and zakāt — then most turned away. A second pledge not to shed their own blood or expel their people is cited; they then do both and ransom some. Those buy this world with the hereafter. Moses received the Book; messengers followed; Jesus son of Mary was given bayyināt and supported with rūḥ al-qudus. Whenever a messenger brought what their souls disliked they grew proud: a party they denied, a party they kill. They say their hearts are wrapped/uncircumcised; God cursed them for kufr. A Book came confirming what is with them; they had sought victory by it; when it came they disbelieved. They sell themselves cheaply. They say we believe what was sent to us and reject what is after — though it is the truth confirming what is with them; then why did you kill the prophets? Moses came with bayyināt; they took the calf. Mountain raised; they said we hear and disobey; the calf was drunk into their hearts. If the Last Abode is exclusive, wish for death — they never will, because of what their hands sent ahead. Gabriel brought the sending-down on “your heart” confirming what was before it; enemy of Gabriel / God / angels / messengers / Michael is answered. Clear signs sent down; covenant thrown behind their backs as if they do not know.
94–96  exclusive hereafter claim tested by wishing death.
Worship none but God; iḥsān to parents, relatives, orphans, the poor; say what is good to people; establish ṣalāh; give zakāt. Then you turned away except a few, while turning aside.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Decalogue / prophetic social law: no other gods; honor parents; care for weak; just speech. Ṣalāh/zakāt are the Quranic cultic pair already commanded in 2:43. See QB-0027.

Pledge: you shall not shed your blood or expel yourselves from your homes. Then you did so, backing one another in sin, and if captives came to you you ransomed them — though expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Book and disbelieve in part? Reward of those who do that: disgrace in this life; harsher punishment on the Day of Rising. They bought worldly life for the hereafter.

DIRECT: partial observance of scripture is itself charged. Medinan tafsir points to Aws/Khazraj Jewish alliances — Level 4 setting, not in the verse. “Believe in part of the Book” thickens QRQ-0003: the issue here is selective practice, not only textual change.

We gave Moses the Book and sent messengers in his track. We gave Jesus son of Mary the bayyināt and supported him with rūḥ al-qudus. Whenever a messenger came with what your souls did not desire, you were arrogant: a party you denied, a party you kill (taqtulūn — imperfect).

DIRECT for QRQ-0002 in canonical order: ʿĪsā ibn Maryam; given clear signs; supported with the holy spirit. No birth, no crucifixion, no deity discussion in this verse. Rūḥ al-qudus: tafsir majority = Gabriel; some = the power by which he raised the dead. Level 1 is the phrase. Christian comparison: Spirit upon Jesus (baptism narratives) is a real overlap of language. Quranic later use of the same Spirit for the Quran’s descent (16:102) pulls the term toward an angel/agency under God. See dossier; QB-0028.
Prophet-killing continues 2:61. Imperfect “you kill” lets the charge include present intent (tafsir often: they will try to kill Muhammad). Level 1 is the verb tense as written.
They say: our hearts are ghulf (covered / uncircumcised / wrapped). Rather, God cursed them for their kufr; little do they believe.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with “uncircumcised heart” in Lev 26:41; Deut 10:16; Jer 4:4; 9:26; Acts 7:51. The Quran puts the slogan in their mouth and answers with curse. See QB-0029.
2:89–91  Confirming Book; we believe only what was sent to us

When a Book from God came confirming what is with them — and they had before sought victory over those who disbelieved — when what they recognized came, they disbelieved. Curse on the disbelievers. Wretched is that for which they sold themselves: disbelief in what God sent down, begrudging that God sends down of His bounty on whom He wills of His servants. When told believe in what God sent down, they say we believe in what was sent down to us, and they disbelieve in what is beyond it, though it is the truth confirming what is with them. Why then did you kill God’s prophets before, if you were believers?

DIRECT: third confirmation clause in this surah (2:41, 2:89, 2:91). The new Book is the truth and muṣaddiq of what they have. Their stated policy is: accept our tanzīl, reject what is after. The Quran treats that as inconsistent with prophet-killing in their past and with the confirming function. Tafsir: they used to ask God for a prophet against the pagans, then rejected Muhammad. That “victory-prayer” story is TAFSIR. Level 1: they had sought victory; when the recognized thing came they disbelieved.
QI-0003 (confirm vs distort) is not resolved; it is thickened. Confirmation language is now repeated against a community charged with killing prophets and discarding covenant (2:101).

Moses came with bayyināt; then you took the calf after him. We raised the mountain; take what We gave you with strength and hear. They said: samiʿnā wa-ʿaṣaynā (we hear and we disobey). The calf was drunk into their hearts by their kufr.
Exodus 24:7 is “we will hear and we will do” (naʿaseh wenišmaʿ). The Quranic pair inverts the obedience half. Whether that is irony, a different memory, or polemic inversion is OPEN. See QB-0030.

If the Last Abode with God is yours alone excluding other people, wish for death if you are truthful. They never will, because of what their hands have sent ahead. You will find them the greediest of people for life, even more than those who associate; one of them would like a thousand years; it would not budge him from the punishment.
A rhetorical test of exclusive-election-plus-hereafter claims. Not a historical census of Jewish longevity wishes.

Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel — he brought it down on your heart by God’s permission, confirming what was before it, guidance and good news for the believers. Whoever is an enemy to God, His angels, His messengers, Gabriel and Michael: God is an enemy to the kāfirīn.

First naming of Jibrīl and Mīkāl. The sending-down is onto “your heart” (the addressee). It confirms what was before it. Asbāb: some Medinan Jews said Gabriel was their enemy (war angel) and Michael a friend — HADITH/SĪRA. Level 1: enmity to Gabriel is enmity to the agent of this tanzīl. Biblical Gabriel/Michael exist (Dan 8–12; Luke 1). See QB-0031.

We sent down clear signs; only the fāsiqūn deny them. Whenever they made a covenant a party of them threw it away. When a messenger from God came confirming what is with them, a party of those given the Book cast the Book of God behind their backs as if they did not know.

Again: confirming what is with them + casting the Book of God behind. Which book is discarded — the Torah they have, or the new confirming Book — is not spelled out. Either reading is possible; both are damning.
binding pledge — same family as ʿahd
holy/pure spirit — referent OPEN at Level 1
confirming what is with them — again
the calf was made to be drunk into their hearts
Holy Spirit / Pure Spirit / Gabriel in notes
Do not print Gabriel as the translation.

Jesus enters the sequential record as a supported messenger with signs in a chain after Moses, against an Israel charged with arrogance toward messengers. Confirmation of prior scripture is now a drumbeat (41, 89, 91, 97, 101). Gabriel is the named down-bringer onto the Prophet’s heart. Partial Book-practice is condemned. Hearts-ghulf and seal/curse continue QI-0001’s agency file.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT (God, parents, weak, speech). Cultic pair is Quranic ṣalāh/zakāt.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT that Jesus is Spirit-supported. Quran does not here identify the Spirit as God.
AGREEMENT on the idiom. Quran places it as their claim and answers with curse.
Hear and disobey vs hear and do
REINTERPRETATION / inversion of the Sinai response formula.
AGREEMENT that both named angels exist. ADDITION: Gabriel as down-bringer of this tanzīl onto the Prophet’s heart. Enmity-to-Gabriel motif is not a biblical Jewish doctrine in that form.
PATTERN thickening of QB-0012. Still no tahrif word in this block.
Medinan address to Jews who have a Book and who, the text says, recognized the new sending-down and still rejected it. Gabriel-enmity belongs to sīra memory of those debates.
Takes covenants; curses for kufr; sends Gabriel; enemy to enemies of His angels.
First sequential hit: Jesus son of Mary, bayyināt, rūḥ al-qudus. Dossier already holds the corpus.
Confirming clauses multiply. Selective practice of the Book condemned (2:85). Covenant discarded (2:101).
Tanzīl via Gabriel, confirming what was before it.
World bought for hereafter → punishment not lightened.
Last Abode not a tribal exclusive; death-wish test.
Confirmation drumbeat vs rejection of what is after “what was sent to us.”
2:83–86 mīthāq + believe part of the Book
2:87 Jesus given bayyināt and supported with rūḥ al-qudus
QB-0027–0031 as table. No new QI number; QI-0003 thickened. QCA-0004 (affirms previous scripture) strengthened again; QCA-0008 (killed prophets) repeated.
New lemmas: mithaq, ruh al-qudus, ghulf, Jibril, Mikal, sami'na wa-asayna.
Jesus dossier: append 2:87 as first canonical-order hit. God: covenants, Gabriel. Muhammad: heart-recipient of Gabriel’s tanzīl.
Victory-prayer story and Gabriel-as-Jewish-enemy: SĪRA/TAFSIR. Rūḥ al-qudus = Gabriel: TAFSIR majority.

Israel’s covenant is restated as worship, family/poor ethics, speech, prayer, alms — then broken. Jesus enters the sequential text as Spirit-supported messenger after Moses. The new Book keeps being called the truth that confirms what they already have; they keep being charged with taking only “what was sent to us” and with killing prophets. Gabriel is named as the one who set the confirming sending-down on the Prophet’s heart.

Next: S002 CP06 = 2:102–112 (Harut/Marut, naskh 2:106 if included, qibla prelude) or 2:102–103 alone if magic needs space, then 2:104–121. Proposed 2:102–113 to keep one packet around naskh + “none will enter garden except Jew or Christian” (2:111) + 2:113 Jews/Christians each deny the other.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP06 vv102-103 Harut Marut
paragraphs: S002 — AL-BAQARAH — CP06  ·  HĀRŪT AND MĀRŪT
Why alone: Owner asked for this narrative. 2:102 is dense enough that folding naskh (2:106) into the same packet would bury it.

They followed what the shayāṭīn recited/recite over the kingdom of Solomon. Solomon did not commit kufr; the shayāṭīn committed kufr. They teach people siḥr (magic/sorcery) and that which was sent down on the two angels at Bābil, Hārūt and Mārūt. Those two do not teach anyone until they say: we are only a fitnah (trial), so do not disbelieve. People learn from them that by which they separate a man and his spouse. They harm no one by it except by God’s permission. They learn what harms them and does not benefit them. They knew that whoever buys it has no share (khalāq) in the hereafter. Wretched is that for which they sold themselves, if they knew.
2:103: If they had believed and been God-fearing, a reward from God would have been better, if they knew.
2. What the verse does not say

It does not narrate: angels volunteering to be tested on earth; a beautiful woman (Zuhra / Venus); wine, fornication, murder; teaching the Greatest Name; hanging upside down in a Babylonian well until the Hour. Those are the “Tale of Hārūt and Mārūt” in tafsir and qiṣaṣ. Provenance: TAFSIR / STORY LITERATURE.
It does not say Solomon practiced magic. It denies his kufr and assigns kufr to the shayāṭīn.
It does not define siḥr. It names one effect: separating spouses. Harm is real only bi-idhn Allāh.
A variant reading malikayn (“two kings”) instead of malakayn (“two angels”) exists in the qirāʾāt discussion. Majority received text: angels. Record the variant as OPEN, not as the base.

ittabaʿū mā tatlū l-shayāṭīnu ʿalā mulki sulaymān. “They” continues the prior Jewish addressees (2:101). Tatlū = recite / follow as recitation. ʿAlā mulki: over / against / during the kingdom. Pickthall hears “falsely related against.” SI hears “during the reign.” Both are live.
wa-mā kafara sulaymānu wa-lākinna l-shayāṭīna kafarū. Explicit exoneration. This is the Quranic answer to a charge that Solomon’s power was sorcery or that Solomon himself disbelieved.

yuʿallimūna l-nāsa l-siḥra wa-mā unzila ʿalā l-malakayni bi-bābila hārūta wa-mārūta. Grammar: “teaching people magic and [teaching] that which was sent down on the two angels” — or “magic, and [they also followed] that which was sent down…” The wa-mā unzila can be coordinated with siḥr or with what the shayāṭīn recited. Either way, something was unzila on two angels in Babylon named Hārūt and Mārūt.
innamā naḥnu fitnatun fa-lā takfur. The angels present their teaching as a test whose wrong use is kufr. Learning the art is possible; practicing it as disbelief is the warned act.
mā yufarriqūna bihi bayna l-marʾi wa-zawjihi. Specified social harm: marriage-rupture magic.
illā bi-idhni llāh. Magic is not an independent rival power.
man ishtarāhu mā lahu fī l-ākhirati min khalāq. Buying this knowledge forfeits a hereafter share. Israel “knew” that — so the charge is against known violation, not ignorance.
4. Solomon in this verse vs the Bible
1 Kings 11:1–13: Solomon loved many foreign women, followed their gods (Ashtoreth, Milcom, Chemosh), and built high places. That is the HB’s own charge of late-life apostasy.

2:102 does not discuss wives or high places. It denies kufr in the specific frame of magic-recitation over his kingdom. Later Quranic Solomon (27; 34; 38) is a believing prophet who commands jinn/winds/birds. Those chapters are not this packet.

QB-0032: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that Solomon is a great king in a world of spirits. DIRECT DENIAL of the idea that Solomon’s power was kufr-sorcery. REINTERPRETATION vs 1 Kings 11 if “kufr” is taken to cover idolatry — the verse’s immediate target is the magic slander, not a line-by-line rebuttal of 1 Kings 11. Do not pretend 2:102 quotes 1 Kings.
5. Fallen-angel and magic lore (comparison, not source-proof)

Genesis 6:1–4: sons of God / daughters of men. 1 Enoch 6–8: Watchers (Shemihazah, Asael/Azazel) teach forbidden arts including “spell-binding and cutting of roots,” cosmetics, weapons; they are bound. Jubilees 5; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6: angels who sinned, kept in chains. Midrashic Shemḥazai and ʿAzael (written forms often medieval): two angels, a woman, loss of the Name, Venus — structurally close to the tafsir Tale, not to 2:102’s short text.

Names Hārūt / Mārūt: often compared with Avestan Haurvatāt and Amərətāt (wholeness / immortality), two Amesha Spentas. That is an etymological hypothesis, not a Quranic footnote. Babylon as location fits a Near Eastern magic capital in late antique imagination.

Solomon + demons is a huge late-antique library (Testament of Solomon; later Jewish and Christian demonology; Islamic jinn-sagas). 2:102 assumes hearers already connect Solomon with spirits and with slander about sorcery.

Classification of the relationship: possible relationship / shared mythic building-blocks (two named teachers of forbidden knowledge; Babylon; marriage harm; test). Demonstrable literary dependence of 2:102 on 1 Enoch or on Midrash Abkir is not established. Reeves and others note that some Jewish “Shemhazai and Azael” written tales post-date Islam and may even echo the Muslim Tale. Direction of traffic is not one-way and not proven for the Quranic verse itself.

QB-0033: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with the Watcher tradition that forbidden knowledge can come via extra-human teachers and destroy human order. ADDITION: the teachers warn “we are a fitnah, do not disbelieve”; harm only by God’s leave; Solomon cleared. OMISSION: sex with human women is not in 2:102.

Kufr can attach to teaching and buying siḥr. Angels can be instruments of a trial that includes dangerous knowledge. God’s permission bounds harm. The hereafter share can be sold. Belief and taqwā (2:103) would have been better than that purchase. This is not a manual of magic; it is a condemnation of following it.
2:14 shayāṭīn; 2:101 discarded Book; later 113–114 jinn; 27 / 34 / 38 Solomon; 113:4 evil of naffāthāt fī l-ʿuqad (women who blow on knots).
Permission-bounds harm; sends down something on two angels as fitnah; better reward if they had believed.
They knew from prior knowledge that buying this has no hereafter share — another “they already knew” clause.
No khalāq in the ākhirah for the buyer.
Solomon did not commit kufr; shayatin did; they teach sihr
Something sent down on two angels in Babylon, Harut and Marut; they warn they are a fitnah
Learned art separates spouses; harm only by God's leave; buyer has no hereafter share
DENIAL of Solomon-as-kafir-sorcerer; 1 Kings 11 idolatry is a different charge
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on forbidden-knowledge angels; tafsir Tale is closer to midrash than 2:102 is
“Solomon was a magician” / “the Quran teaches fallen-angel fornication at Babylon”
First is what 2:102 denies. Second is tafsir, not the verse.
sihr; fitnah; Babil; Harut; Marut; khalaq; tala (recite).
Dossier_Solomon opened from this verse: prophet-king, not kafir, kingdom associated with shayatin recitation that he is cleared of.
Provenance split is the point of this packet. Do not quote Tabari’s woman-and-well as “the Quranic story of Harut and Marut.”

No extra-Quranic 7th-century inscription of these two names in a magic-teacher pair is cited here. Babylon as a magic topos is historically real as reputation. The verse is not an archaeological report.

2:102 is a polemic clearing Solomon and condemning those who followed devil-recitation and Babylon-sent teaching that breaks marriages. The angels warn that the teaching is a trial and that using it is kufr. Later Muslim storytelling filled in a Watcher-style romance that the verse does not tell. Biblical 1 Kings charges Solomon with idolatry, not this magic slander; Enoch charges Watchers with teaching forbidden arts and with sex — only the first theme is close to 2:102’s wording.
Next sequential: 2:104–113 (or through 2:121), including naskh (2:106) and “none enter the Garden except Jew or Christian” (2:111).

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP07 vv104-121
paragraphs: Why this cut: From raʿinā / naskh through millah-pressure. 2:122 repeats 2:47 and opens another Israel block.

Believers are told not to say raʿinā but unẓurnā. People of the Book who disbelieve and the mushrikūn do not want good sent down to “you.” Whatever sign We naskh or cause to be forgotten, We bring better or like it. Do not question your messenger as Moses was questioned. Many People of the Book want to turn you back after faith, out of envy. Prayer and zakāt. They say none enter the Garden except a Jew or a Christian — amānī; produce your proof. Whoever aslama his face to God and is muḥsin has his reward, no fear, no grief. Jews say Christians stand on nothing; Christians say Jews stand on nothing; both recite the Book. Who is more unjust than one who bars God’s mosques? East and west are God’s; wherever you turn, there is God’s face. They say God has taken a son; glory to Him; all in the heavens and earth is His, all qānit. Originator; when He decrees, He says kun fa-yakūn. Why does God not speak to us or a sign come? We sent you with the truth as bringer of good news and warner. Jews and Christians will never be pleased with you until you follow their millah; God’s guidance is the guidance. Those given the Book who recite it as it should be recited — those believe in it.

Do not say raʿinā; say unẓurnā and listen. Tafsir (and 4:46 later): a word that in Arabic can mean “attend to us” and can be twisted toward insult. Level 1 here is a speech-discipline command to believers. The Hebrew-insult story is TAFSIR until 4:46 is read.
Mā nansakh min āyatin aw nunsihā naʾti bi-khayrin minhā aw mithlihā. Whatever āyah We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring one better than it or like it. God is able over all things.

This is the project’s first explicit naskh verse. Āyah can mean a recitation-unit or a sign. Classical uṣūl made this the engine of legal abrogation inside the Quran and sometimes of prior law. Level 1: God replaces some āyāt with better or equal ones, and can make some forgotten. It does not list which verses, does not say “the Torah is abrogated in full,” and does not say every later verse cancels every earlier one. That expansion is legal theory (Level 4–5). See QDISC-0041, QCA-0011.

Or do you want to question your messenger as Moses was questioned before? Whoever exchanges faith for kufr has strayed from the even way. Biblical analogue: Israel’s testing at Massah/Meribah and “is the Lord among us?” (Exod 17; Num 14). PARTIAL AGREEMENT on the motif of over-questioning a messenger.
Many of the People of the Book want to turn you back after your faith as kāfirīn, out of ḥasad after the truth became clear. Pardon and overlook until God comes with His command.
2:111–113 exclusive Garden; each denies the other

They said: none will enter the Garden except one who is a Jew or a Christian. Those are their amānī. Produce your burhān if you are truthful. No: whoever submits his face to God and is a doer of good — his reward is with his Lord; no fear, no grief. The Jews say the Christians are not on anything; the Christians say the Jews are not on anything; they recite the Book. Those who do not know say the like of their saying. God will judge between them on the Day of Rising.

DIRECT: an exclusive communal ticket to the Garden is rejected as wish. The replacement condition is aslama wajhahu lillāh + iḥsān — same no-fear/no-grief cadence as 2:38 and 2:62. 2:62 named Jews and Christians inside a reward formula; 2:111 rejects Jewish-or-Christian exclusivism. That is complementary more than contradictory: 2:62 conditions reward on God, Last Day, and ṣāliḥ work, not on the communal badge. 2:113 is a sharp intra-People-of-the-Book observation: each nullifies the other while both recite scripture. See QI-0004 note: 2:62 vs later 3:85 still pending; 2:111 is not 3:85.

QB-0034: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that rival communities claim exclusive salvation (cf. some Jewish election language; extra ecclesiam nulla salus in later Christian form). The Quran refuses the badge-only version.

Who is more unjust than one who prevents God’s mosques so that His name not be remembered in them and strives to ruin them? They should not enter them except in fear. To God belong east and west; wherever you turn, there is the face (wajh) of God.
2:115 is later used in qibla debates (2:142ff). Here it is a universal-direction statement. Anthropomorphic “face” is the wording; later kalām will qualify it.

They say God has taken a walad. Glory to Him. Rather, to Him belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; all are qānitūn. Originator of the heavens and the earth; when He decrees a matter He only says to it “be,” and it is.

“They” is unspecified in this verse (Jews / Christians / pagans all appear in nearby tafsir). Christian “Son of God” is the main comparison target. 9:30 will later name ʿUzayr and the Messiah separately. Level 1 here: taking a son is denied; creative speech is kun. QB-0021 thickened. DIRECT CONTRADICTION with ontological sonship remains.

We sent you with the truth as mubashshir and nadhīr. You will not be asked about the companions of Hell. Never will the Jews be pleased with you, nor the Christians, until you follow their millah. Say: God’s guidance is the guidance. If you follow their desires after knowledge has come to you, you have no protector or helper from God.

Millah = religion / rite-community. This is the hardest sentence in the block toward living Jews and Christians as communities: pleasure is conditioned on joining their millah. It does not say every Jew or Christian is damned; it says communal approval of “you” will not come short of conversion to their rite. Pair with 2:62 and 2:112 rather than letting 2:120 erase them.
Those to whom We gave the Book, yatlūnahu ḥaqqa tilāwatihi — those believe in it. Whoever disbelieves in it, those are the losers.

A positive class among Book-recipients: they recite it with its due recitation and believe. Thickens the split already in 2:75–79 (distorters / writers / ummiyyūn / now proper reciters). QRQ-0003 is not a single Jewish-Christian blob.
abrogate / cause to forget — first naskh lemma
sign or recitation unit — both live
Be, and it is — same creative formula as Jesus/Adam later

God replaces āyāt; owns east and west; has no son; creates by speech; will judge between Book-communities; His guidance is the guidance. Salvation language in 2:112 is submission + iḥsān, not a communal brand.
2:111 exclusive Garden vs communal election / extra ecclesiam
REINTERPRETATION: badge-only ticket refused; 2:112 condition stated
2:113 each community nullifies the other while reciting scripture
ADDITION as a Quranic social observation; no single Bible verse is the source
DIRECT CONTRADICTION with ontological Sonship; “they” unspecified here
Tension with irenic readings of 2:62; not a contradiction inside 2:62 itself
No son; kun-creator; naskh-agent; face everywhere; judge between communities.
Sonship denied without naming Jesus in 2:116.
2:121 proper reciters believe; 2:113 both recite while denying each other.
Naskh of āyāt; tanzīl of good they do not want.
2:62 still on the table; 2:111–120 harden communal conflict without cancelling 2:62’s wording.
2:104–105 ra'ina; People of the Book and mushrikun begrudge tanzil
2:106 naskh / forget an ayah; bring better or like it
2:111–113 exclusive Garden refused; each Book-community nullifies the other
2:116–117 God has not taken a son; kun fa-yakun
2:120 Jews and Christians will not be pleased until you follow their millah
2:121 some given the Book recite it with its due recitation and believe

QCA-0011: “Naskh means the Quran cancelled the Bible.” 2:106 talks about āyāt God naskhs or causes to be forgotten and replaces. Applying that automatically to the entire prior canon is a further step.
QI-0004 still reserved for 2:62 vs 3:85. 2:111 is a rejection of exclusivism, which actually sits nearer 2:62 than 3:85 does.

God claims the right to replace revelations, refuses a Jew-or-Christian ticket as the definition of the Garden, denies that He took a son, and tells the addressee that Jewish and Christian pleasure will not come short of following their millah. At the same time, some who were given the Book recite it properly and believe, and whoever submits his face and does good has the 2:38/2:62 reward formula. Those lines have to travel together.
Next: 2:122–141 (Israel favor reprise; Abraham’s trial, House, millat Ibrāhīm — a comparison-heavy Abraham block).

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP08 vv122-141
paragraphs: Why this cut: Abraham / House / millat Ibrāhīm argument closes at 2:141. 2:142 opens the qibla.
Comparison priority: Who owns Abraham; Ishmael at the House; creed that names Jesus beside Moses.

Israel is again told to remember favor and preference, and to fear a Day when no soul avails another (near-repeat of 2:47–48). Abraham is tried with words, fulfills them, and is made imām for the people; the covenant will not reach the ẓālimīn. The House is made a resort and security; the standing-place of Abraham a prayer-place; Abraham and Ishmael are charged to purify the House. Abraham asks for a secure town and fruit for its people who believe. He and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House and pray to be muslimīn, for a muslim nation from their seed, and for a messenger from among them who will recite signs, teach the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Turning from Abraham’s millah is folly. Abraham charged his sons, and Jacob: do not die except as muslimūn. Jacob at death: what will you worship after me? We will worship your God and the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac — one God; we are muslimūn. That was a nation that has passed; you will not be asked about what they did. They say: be Jews or Christians and you will be guided. Say: rather the millah of Abraham the ḥanīf; he was not of the mushrikīn. Creed: we believe in God and what was sent down to us and to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the tribes, and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets; we make no distinction; we are muslimūn. If they believe like that, they are guided; if they turn away, they are in schism. Ṣibghat Allāh. Will you argue with us about God when He is our Lord and yours? That nation has passed.
Same pair as 2:47–48 with a small word-order shift on intercession/ransom. QI-0002 (intercession) is not new here.
2:124 Abraham tried; imām; covenant not for ẓālimīn
When Abraham’s Lord tried him with kalimāt and he fulfilled them, He said: I am making you an imām for the people. Abraham: and from my offspring? He: My covenant does not reach the ẓālimīn.

PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Gen 12; 15; 17; 22: election after trial, blessing for nations, covenant. The words of the trial are unnamed here (later tradition lists rites). ADDITION: explicit “not for the wrongdoers” limit on the covenant’s reach through the seed — a theological brake on ethnic automaticity. See QB-0037.

The House (al-bayt) is made a return-place and security. Take maqām Ibrāhīm as a muṣallā. Abraham and Ishmael: purify My House for ṭawāf, ʿākifīn, rukūʿ and sujūd. Abraham’s prayer: make this a secure town; provide fruit to its people who believe in God and the Last Day (God: and whoever disbelieves I will let enjoy a little then the Fire). Raising the foundations: Our Lord accept; make us two muslims to You and from our seed a muslim ummah; show us our rites; relent. Send among them a messenger from them who recites Your signs, teaches the Book and ḥikmah, and purifies them.

This is the project’s first Kaʿba/House narrative. Genesis has Abraham at Shechem, Bethel, Hebron, Moriah — not Mecca, and not building a house with Ishmael. Ishmael in Genesis 16–21 is the son sent away; the covenant line is named through Isaac (Gen 17:19–21; 21:12). 2:127 puts Ishmael beside Abraham as co-raiser of the House’s foundations and co-pray-er for a messenger from “them.”

QB-0038: ADDITION relative to the HB narrative geography. Possible relationship to post-biblical Abraham-Ishmael expansions is OPEN (Witztum and others have argued a link to aqedah traditions relocated). Not demonstrable copying of a single known Jewish text about building the Kaʿba.
The prayed-for messenger “from them” is unnamed. Pattern-reading = Muhammad. Level 1: a messenger from that seed who teaches Book and wisdom.

Who turns from Abraham’s millah except one who fools himself? Abraham charged his sons, and Jacob: God has chosen this dīn for you; do not die except as muslimūn. Were you witnesses when death came to Jacob? What will you worship after me? Your God and the God of your fathers Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac — one God; we are muslimūn to Him. That ummah has passed; it has what it earned; you have what you earn.

Jacob’s deathbed in Gen 49 is blessing-poems over the tribes, not this creed-question. The Quranic scene is a monotheism-and-submission last will. Ishmael is listed among “your fathers” with Isaac — a genealogical grouping Genesis does not use for Jacob’s sons (Ishmael is uncle, not father). See QB-0039.
2:135–141 millat Ibrāhīm vs Jew or Christian

They say: be Jews or Christians and you will be guided. Say: rather millat Ibrāhīm ḥanīfan; he was not of the mushrikīn. Then the creed of 2:136: God; what was sent down to us; what was sent down to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the asbāṭ; what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets; no distinction; we are muslimūn. If they believe with the like of what you believe, they are guided; if they turn away, they are in shiqāq. Ṣibghat Allāh — and who is better at coloring than God? We are ʿābidūn. Do you argue with us about God while He is our Lord and yours, and we have our deeds and you have yours? Or do you say Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the tribes were Jews or Christians? Say: are you more knowing, or God? That ummah has passed.
