This is the block’s thesis: Abraham is neither Jew nor Christian (those labels are later); he is ḥanīf, not a mushrik; the living path is his millah. 2:136 names Jesus in the same breath as Moses inside a no-distinction creed — important for QRQ-0002 and 0010. “No distinction” here is about accepting all those prophets, not about collapsing their messages into identity.

QB-0040: REINTERPRETATION of Abrahamic ownership. Paul (Rom 4; Gal 3) also claims Abraham beyond Torah-ethnicity. The Quran claims him beyond both Judaism and Christianity as later millahs. Structural similarity of “Abraham as prior-to-your-label”; content differs (ḥanīf / millah / House / Ishmael).
the House — later identified as the Kaʿba
submitters — here a self-description of Abraham’s line, not the later demonym only
inclining (to one God) / upright; not of the mushrikīn
we do not distinguish (among those prophets)

Abraham is the imām whose millah predates Jewish and Christian labels. The House is Abraham-and-Ishmael work. A messenger is prayed from that seed. Jesus is inside the one-prophet-list. Dead generations do not save the living.
No Meccan House in Genesis; Ishmael sent away
ADDITION of sacred geography; REINTERPRETATION of Ishmael’s role
REINTERPRETATION (creed vs tribal poems); Ishmael listed among fathers
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on pre-label Abraham; different positive content (hanif, House, Ishmael)
2:136 names Jesus in the no-distinction list
PATTERN: Jesus is a given-to prophet among others in this creed
Tries Abraham; limits covenant; owns the House; will send a messenger from that seed (prayer).
Jesus in 2:136 list with Moses; no extra Christology here.
What was sent down to Abraham’s line and given to Moses and Jesus is to be believed together.
Unnamed messenger from Abraham-Ishmael seed prayed in 2:129.
Millat Ibrahim as the third path vs be-Jews-or-Christians.
2:124 Abraham tried; imam; covenant not for zalimin
2:125–129 House; Ishmael co-builder; prayer for a messenger from them
2:130–134 millah handed down; Jacob’s sons as muslimun
2:135–140 millat Ibrahim hanif vs Jew or Christian; 2:136 creed including Jesus

Abraham is claimed as a ḥanīf imām whose millah is neither Judaism nor Christianity as later labels. Ishmael stands with him at the House. Isaac and Jacob remain in the line. Jesus sits in the same “what was given to the prophets” list as Moses. The living are not saved by the dead nation’s file.
The binding of the son (37:100–113) is not in this block. Do not decide Isaac-vs-Ishmael from 2:122–141.
Next: 2:142–167 (qibla change — comparison-light legally, heavy for identity). Or 2:142–152 if kept tight.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP09 vv142-162
paragraphs: Why this cut: Qibla unit + Safa/Marwa + slain-not-dead + concealers’ curse. 2:163 starts a tawhid/creation hymn.

The foolish will ask what turned them from their former qibla. East and west are God’s. You were made a midmost ummah to be witnesses over people, the messenger a witness over you. The former qibla was appointed to know who follows the messenger. We have seen your face turning in the sky; We will turn you to a qibla you please: face the Sacred Mosque; wherever you are, face it. Those given the Book know it is the truth from their Lord. Even if you brought every sign they would not follow your qibla, nor you theirs, nor they one another’s. Those given the Book recognize it as they recognize their sons; a party conceals the truth. Each has a direction. Wherever you go, face the Sacred Mosque so that people have no ḥujjah against you except the ẓālimūn. As We sent among you a messenger from you who recites, purifies, teaches Book and wisdom — remember Me; I remember you. Seek help in patience and prayer. Do not say of those slain in God’s way that they are dead; they are alive but you do not perceive. We will test you with fear, hunger, loss; give good news to the patient who say we belong to God and to Him we return. Ṣafā and Marwah are among God’s shaʿāʾir; ṭawāf between them is no sin (and voluntary good is rewarded). Those who conceal what We sent down of clear proofs and guidance, after We made it clear in the Book — God curses them and the cursers, except those who repent. Those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers: curse of God, angels, and people, abiding.

Level 1: there was a qibla they used to be on; it is being left; the new orientation is al-masjid al-ḥarām; God owns east and west (echo 2:115). The former qibla is a test of who follows the messenger. People of the Book will not adopt this qibla; you will not adopt theirs; they do not follow one another’s.

Sīra/hadith: first Medinan orientation was Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), then Kaʿba. That identification of the old qibla is not named in 2:142–145. It is the standard historical reading and should stay tagged TRADITION unless a later verse names Jerusalem. 2:144 “a qibla you will be pleased with” plus the face-in-the-sky is the only motive the text gives.

Bible comparison: Jewish prayer toward Jerusalem is biblical (1 Kgs 8:29–30, 44; Dan 6:10). Christian orientation later varies (eastward churches). The Quranic move is a sacred-geography transfer from the Israelite axis (if the old qibla is Jerusalem) to the House of 2:125–129. QB-0041: REINTERPRETATION of which sanctuary is the living center. Not a contradiction of 1 Kings 8; it is a rival claim of center.
You were made a midmost/just nation to be witnesses over people, and the messenger a witness over you. Witness language will return in other surahs. Wasaṭ = middle, just, balanced — range is real.
2:146 recognize it as they recognize their sons

Those whom We gave the Book recognize it (yaʿrifūnahu) as they recognize their sons. A party conceals the truth while they know. The pronoun “it” can be the new direction, the messenger, or the Book — Arabic is not explicit. All three sit in tafsir. Level 1: recognition-as-of-sons + knowing concealment. Thickens 2:42, 2:75, 2:146 as a concealment pattern. QI-0003 still open.
2:148–150 each community a direction; no ḥujjah

Each has a wijha he turns to; so race to good. Facing the Sacred Mosque wherever you are, so the people will have no argument against you except those who do wrong. Do not fear them; fear Me. I complete My favor.

A messenger from you recites Our signs, purifies you, teaches the Book and wisdom and what you did not know. That is the content Abraham and Ishmael asked for in 2:129. Pattern-identification of the addressee with that prayed messenger is now very strong. Still not the proper name Muhammad.

Do not say of those killed in God’s way “amwāt.” Rather living, but you do not feel it. Testing with fear, hunger, loss of money, lives, crops. Good news to the ṣābirīn who say innā lillāhi wa-innā ilayhi rājiʿūn. Blessings and mercy on those.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with martyr-alive motifs (cf. 2 Maccabees; some NT “to live is Christ”). The Quranic wording is this-world command: do not call them dead. Later theology of barzakh is extra.
They are among God’s waymarks. Whoever makes ḥajj or ʿumrah to the House, there is no junāḥ on him to circuit between them. Whoever does good voluntarily — God is thankful, knowing.

Sīra: some hesitated because the run was a pre-Islamic rite. That hesitation is not in the verse. Level 1: the two hills are authorized as shaʿāʾir; ṭawāf between them is permitted, not described as invented.

Those who conceal what We sent down of bayyināt and guidance after We made it clear to people in the Book — God curses them and those who curse, except who repent, put right, and make clear. Those who disbelieve and die as disbelievers: curse of God, angels, and people together; abiding; punishment not lightened.
Strongest concealment-curse so far. Exception for tawbah that includes making-clear. Dying on kufr locks the curse. Pair with 2:121 (proper reciters) so the Book-people are still not one block.
the sacred mosque — House complex of 2:125
recognize it as they recognize their sons
we belong to God and to Him we return
Change of sacred direction vs Jerusalem prayer (1 Kgs 8; Dan 6:10)
REINTERPRETATION of the living center if old qibla = Jerusalem (tradition). Text itself does not name Jerusalem.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with some Jewish/Christian martyr-alive language; not identical to resurrection-on-the-third-day.
Owns east and west; appoints and changes qibla; tests followers; remembers those who remember Him; curses concealers.
Recognize-as-sons; conceal after We made it clear in the Book; tawbah must make clear.
Messenger from you; 2:129 prayer content now described as sent.
Qibla change as authorized replacement of a prior practice — cousin of naskh (2:106), not named naskh here.
Slain in God's way are living; dying on kufr → abiding curse.
People of the Book will not share this qibla; they do not share one another's.
Qibla turned to the Sacred Mosque; former qibla was a test
DIRECT; old target unnamed in verse
Those given the Book recognize it as their sons; a party conceals
Slain in God's way are living; Safa and Marwa are sha'a'ir
Concealers of sent-down proofs cursed unless they repent and make clear

Worship direction is moved to the Sacred Mosque of the Abraham-Ishmael House. The old direction is treated as a completed test. People of the Book are said to know this is truth and still not share the qibla. Concealment after clarification draws a curse that tawbah can lift if it includes making-clear. The slain are not to be called dead.
Next: 2:163–177 (one God; rivals; righteousness defined beyond turning faces east or west — 2:177 is a major ethics verse) or 2:163–177 as one packet.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP10 vv163-177
paragraphs: Why this cut: Tawhid hymn through the definition of birr. 2:178 opens qiṣāṣ.

Your God is one God; no god but He, the All-Merciful. In the creation of heavens and earth, night and day, the ship, rain, beasts, winds and clouds are signs for people who reason. Some take rivals (andād) and love them as they love God; those who believe love God more intensely. When the followed see the punishment they will disown the followers. Eat of what is on earth ḥalāl ṭayyib; do not follow Satan’s footsteps. He commands indecency and that you say about God what you do not know. When it is said follow what God sent down, they say we follow what we found our fathers on — even if their fathers understood nothing. The kāfir likeness: a shepherd calling what hears only a shout. Eat of the good We provided; be grateful. He has only forbidden carrion, blood, swine-flesh, and what was dedicated to other than God — unless compelled without desire or transgression. Those who conceal what God sent down of the Book and sell it for a small price eat fire. God sent down the Book in truth; those who differ over the Book are in far schism. Birr is not turning faces toward east or west. Birr is one who believes in God, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets; gives wealth despite love of it to kin, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask, and for freeing necks; establishes prayer and zakāt; keeps the promise; is patient in misery, hardship, and battle. Those are the truthful; those are the muttaqūn.

Ilāhukum ilāhun wāḥidun. Cosmological list: heavens/earth, night/day, ship that runs with benefit, water from the sky that revives the earth, beasts, winds and clouds musakhkhar between sky and earth. Signs for a people who reason. This is natural theology, not a narrative.

Some take rivals besides God and love them as God’s love. Believers love God more intensely. When they see the punishment, the followed will disown the followers; bonds are cut; they wish they could return and disown as they were disowned. Deeds shown as ḥasarāt; they will not leave the Fire.
Andād can be idols, leaders, or desires. The scene is eschatological regret, not a census of Meccan cults.

Addressed first to people (yā-ayyuhā l-nās), then to believers. Lawful and good vs Satan’s footsteps. Ancestral custom is not a proof if the fathers did not reason. Four prohibitions only in this verse: mayta, blood, flesh of swine, and what was offered to other than God. Necessity exception: not desiring, not transgressing.

QB-0043 vs Leviticus 11 / Deut 14: PARTIAL AGREEMENT on blood, carrion, swine, and dedication-to-other-gods. OMISSION of the long clean/unclean species list, mixing, and other Levitical fences. Acts 15:20, 29 keeps blood, strangled, idols for Gentiles — closer in brevity to 2:173 than Lev 11 is. Do not call 2:173 a copy of Acts 15; both are short prohibition lists in a larger food-law world.

Those who conceal what God sent down of the Book and purchase with it a small price: they eat fire into their bellies. God will not speak to them on the Day of Rising nor purify them. They bought error with guidance. Because God sent down the Book with truth; those who differ about the Book are in far schism.
Repeats 2:79 / 2:159 with “eat fire.” The Book is sent down in truth even while people differ over it — another confirm-and-conflict pair for QI-0003.

Laysa l-birra an tuwallū wujūhakum qibala l-mashriqi wa-l-maghribi. After two packets of qibla argument, righteousness is defined as not identical with the compass-point. Then a list: creed (God, Last Day, angels, the Book, the prophets) + wealth given despite love of it (six recipients including freeing necks) + prayer and zakāt + keeping ʿahd + ṣabr in misery, disease/hardship, and war. Those are ṣadaqū; those are the muttaqūn.

QB-0044: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with prophetic critiques of rite without justice (Isa 1:11–17; Amos 5:21–24; Mic 6:6–8; Hos 6:6; Matt 23; Jas 1:27). The Quran does not abolish qibla (it just commanded it); it refuses to let direction be the definition of birr. ADDITION: the specific five-point creed including angels and “the Book.”
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 11 / Deut 14 on the four; OMISSION of the long species code; brevity nearer Acts 15 than Leviticus
Birr is not east or west (2:177)
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with prophet/Gospel critiques of rite-without-justice; qibla is not abolished
One God; signs in creation; more loved than rivals; sent the Book in truth; forbids four foods with necessity exception.
Conceal-and-sell the Book; differ over the Book in far schism.
2:177 is a full righteousness definition: creed + gift + cult + covenant + patience.
Ancestral custom is not proof; Satan commands saying about God what you do not know.
2:177 names the prophets as a class inside birr — includes prior messengers without ranking them here.
2:163–167 one God; signs; rivals loved as God
2:168–173 four food prohibitions + necessity; ancestral custom insufficient
2:174–176 conceal and sell the Book; eat fire
2:177 birr is not east or west but creed + gift + prayer/zakat + promise + sabr

After commanding a new qibla, the surah refuses to let compass-points define righteousness. Birr is creed, costly giving, prayer, alms, kept promises, and patience under fire. Food law in this unit is short: four bans and a necessity clause. Concealment-for-price of the Book is again fire in the belly.
Next: 2:178–188 (qiṣāṣ, bequest, fasting Ramaḍān) — first long legal panel of the surah.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP11 vv178-195
paragraphs: Why this cut: First legal panel: qiṣāṣ, bequest, Ramaḍān, property, then first fighting cluster. 2:196 opens ḥajj detail.

Qiṣāṣ is prescribed in the slain: free for free, slave for slave, female for female. Remission by brother accepted with payment in iḥsān is a mercy; transgression after that is a painful punishment. In qiṣāṣ is life. Prescribed: when death approaches and he leaves good, a bequest for parents and relatives with maʿrūf — a duty on the muttaqīn. Changing it after hearing it: sin on the changers. If one fears error or sin from a testator and makes peace, no sin. Fasting is prescribed as it was prescribed on those before you, that you may become muttaqūn — limited days; sick or traveling make up later; those who can manage it with hardship: fidya of feeding a poor person; voluntary extra is better; fasting is better if you knew. Ramaḍān is the month in which the Quran was sent down as guidance, bayyināt, and furqān. Whoever is present, fast it; sick or traveling, a number of other days. God wants ease, not hardship, and that you complete the number and magnify God for having guided you. When My servants ask you about Me: I am near; I answer the caller when he calls. So let them respond to Me and believe, that they may be guided. Permitted on fasting nights: approach your women; they are a garment for you and you for them. God knew you were betraying yourselves and relented. Eat and drink until the white thread of dawn is distinct from the black, then complete the fast to night. Do not have intercourse while you are ʿākifūn in mosques. These are God’s limits. Do not consume one another’s property by false means or send it to judges to consume a portion of others’ property in sin. They ask about new moons: they are time-marks for people and ḥajj. Piety is not entering houses from their backs; enter them by their doors. Fight in God’s way those who fight you; do not transgress; God does not love transgressors. Kill them wherever you come upon them and expel them from where they expelled you; fitnah is worse than killing. Do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there; if they fight you, kill them — recompense of the kāfirīn. If they cease, God is forgiving, merciful. Fight them until there is no fitnah and the dīn is for God; if they cease, no ʿudwān except against the ẓālimīn. Sacred month for sacred month; violations have qiṣāṣ; whoever aggresses against you, aggress against him with the like; fear God. Spend in God’s way; do not throw yourselves into destruction with your own hands; do good.

Prescribed in the qatlā. Matching categories: ḥurr/ḥurr, ʿabd/ʿabd, unthā/unthā. A brother may remit; payment with iḥsān follows. After remission, transgression is punished. In qiṣāṣ is life, that you may become muttaqūn.

QB-0045: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with lex talionis (Exod 21:23–25; Lev 24:19–20; Deut 19:21). ADDITION of explicit brother-remission and “in qiṣāṣ is life.” NT trajectory in Matt 5:38–39 is a different ethic (do not resist the evildoer). Record both: HB parallel is the closer legal analogue; Sermon on the Mount is a contrast, not a source.

When death is near and good is left, a waṣiyya for parents and nearest kin with maʿrūf. Changing a heard bequest: sin on the changer. Peacemaking when error or sin is feared: no sin. Later inheritance verses (4:11–12) will interact with this; do not import them yet as if 2:180 were already abrogated. Naskh of bequest-by-heirs is a later uṣūl claim (Level 4).

Fasting prescribed as on those before you — an explicit continuity claim with prior communities. Purpose: taqwā. Limited days; illness and travel: qaḍāʾ. Hardship option: fidya of feeding a poor person; extra good is better; fasting still preferred. Ramaḍān named as the month of the Quran’s tanzīl — guidance, clear proofs, criterion. Present in the month: fast it. Ease not hardship; complete the number; magnify God.
2:186: when they ask you about Me — I am near; I answer the caller. No mediator is named.

2:187: nights of the fast, sexual approach is permitted; garment metaphor; a prior self-betrayal God relented from (asbāb: some thought nights were also forbidden — TAFSIR). Dawn thread; complete to night; no intercourse in iʿtikāf. Ḥudūd Allāh.

QB-0046: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that fasting is an inherited rite (Lev 16; Zech 8; Matt 6:16–18; pre-Islamic and Jewish fasts). ADDITION: this month is named Ramaḍān and identified as the Quran’s descent-month. The “as it was prescribed on those before you” is Level 1 continuity; it does not specify which prior calendar.
Do not eat property among yourselves by bāṭil, nor send it to ḥukkām in order to eat a portion of people’s property in sin while you know. Legal ethics: bribery / abusive litigation.
Ahilla are mawāqīt for people and ḥajj. Birr is not entering houses from their backs. Enter by doors; fear God. Another anti-formalism line after 2:177.

Level 1, without later fiqh expansion: fight in God’s way those who fight you; do not transgress; God does not love those who transgress. Kill/expel in reciprocity of expulsion; fitnah is worse than killing. No fighting at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there; if they do, kill them; if they cease, God is forgiving. Fight until there is no fitnah and the dīn is for God; if they cease, no assault except on the ẓālimīn. Sacred month answers sacred month; ḥurumāt have qiṣāṣ; answer aggression with its like. Spend; do not throw yourselves to tahluka with your own hands; iḥsān.
Fitnah here is usually read as persecution / forced apostasy / sedition — range is real. “Dīn is for God” is a purpose-clause, not a detailed constitution.

QB-0047: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with HB war law that includes reciprocal ḥerem, sacred-time limits, and “eye for eye” at community scale (Deut 20 is harsher in places; Exod 21 is the talion frame). CONTRAST with Matt 5:39 and with later just-war theory that is not in this verse. Do not flatten 2:190–193 into either “only defensive forever” or “open-ended conquest.” The verses contain both a against-those-who-fight-you limiter (190) and an until-fitnah-ceases purpose (193). How those two clauses govern each other is the live uṣūl fight. Level 1 records both clauses.
This packet describes the text. It is not a targeting guide.
do not throw yourselves to destruction
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Exod 21 / Lev 24 / Deut 19; CONTRAST Matt 5:38–39; ADDITION of remission-as-mercy
Fasting as prior prescription; Ramadan as tanzil month
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on fasting as inherited; ADDITION of named month + Quran descent
Fight those who fight you; fitnah worse than killing
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with reciprocal HB war frames; two clauses (190 limiter / 193 purpose) must both stay visible
Near; answers the caller; wants ease; relents; does not love transgressors; with the muttaqin.
Quran sent down in Ramadan as guidance, proofs, furqan.
Qisas, bequest, fasting rules, property/judges, fighting limits and purposes, sacred-month reciprocity.
In qisas is life; if they cease God is forgiving; do not throw yourselves to destruction.
Qisas prescribed; remission; in qisas is life
Bequest for parents and kin with ma'ruf
Fasting prescribed as on those before; Ramadan is tanzil month; God is near
Fight those who fight you; no transgression; fitnah worse than killing; until din is for God

Law arrives in a cluster: equivalent retaliation with a mercy-offramp, a deathbed bequest, a fast like those before you now pinned to Ramaḍān as the Quran’s month, a near God who answers, then a fight-cluster that both limits combat to those who fight you and states a purpose until fitnah is gone and dīn is God’s. Both clauses belong in the record.
Next: 2:196–203 (ḥajj / ʿumrah) then 2:204–214, or 2:196–214 if kept as one pilgrimage-plus-hypocrite packet.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP12 vv196-214
paragraphs: Complete ḥajj and ʿumrah for God. If prevented, an easy hady; do not shave until it reaches its place; illness or head-harm: fidya of fast or charity or offering. When secure: tamattuʿ ʿumrah-to-ḥajj with easy hady; if none, fast three days in ḥajj and seven when you return — ten complete. For those whose family is not resident at the Sacred Mosque. Ḥajj is in known months; whoever undertakes it: no rafath, no fusūq, no jidāl. Take provision; the best provision is taqwā. No sin to seek bounty from your Lord. When you pour down from ʿArafāt, remember God at the sacred mashʿar; remember Him as He guided you, though you were before of those astray. Then pour from where the people pour and ask forgiveness. When you have completed your rites, remember God as you remember your fathers or more intensely. Some say: our Lord give us in this world — they have no share in the hereafter. Some say: give us good in this world and good in the hereafter and protect us from the Fire — those have a share of what they earned. Remember God in numbered days; whoever hurries in two days, no sin; whoever delays, no sin, for one who fears. Among people is one whose worldly speech pleases you, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, while he is the fiercest of disputers; when he turns away he strives in the land to corrupt and destroy crops and stock; God does not love corruption. When he is told fear God, pride in sin takes him. Among people is one who sells himself seeking God’s pleasure. O believers, enter into al-silm completely; do not follow Satan’s footsteps. If you slip after clear proofs, know God is mighty, wise. Do they wait for God to come to them in canopies of clouds with the angels? Ask the Children of Israel how many a clear sign We gave them. Whoever exchanges God’s blessing after it has come — God is severe in punishment. The life of this world is zīna for those who disbelieve; they ridicule those who believe; those who fear will be above them on the Day of Rising. Mankind was one ummah; then God sent prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people in what they differed. Only those who were given it differed in it after clear proofs, out of baghy among themselves. God guided those who believed to the truth of what they differed in, by His leave. God guides whom He wills to a straight path. Or did you think you would enter the Garden while there has not yet come to you the like of those who passed before you? Hardship and suffering touched them and they were shaken until the messenger and those who believed with him said: when is God’s help? Unquestionably God’s help is near.

Legal skeleton: complete both rites for God; iḥṣār (prevention) → easy offering; no shaving until the offering arrives; head-fidya menu; tamattuʿ with offering or 3+7 fast; residents of the Ḥaram excepted from that tamattuʿ rule. Known months. Iḥrām bans: rafath, fusūq, jidāl. Provision / taqwā. Trade during ḥajj not sinful. Pouring from ʿArafāt; remember God at the sacred mashʿar; pour from where people pour. Remember God after rites as you remember fathers or more. Two prayers: world-only vs world-and-hereafter-and-Fire. Numbered days; two-day haste or delay both allowed for the muttaqī.

This is the first detailed ḥajj code. Geography (ʿArafāt, mashʿar) is Arabian. QB-0048: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with pilgrimage-and-sacrifice structures in the Torah (ḥag, ʿolah, firstfruits, booths). OMISSION of Jerusalem/Temple as the site. ADDITION of ʿumrah, iḥrām bans in this wording, ʿArafāt. Not a rewrite of Leviticus 23; it is a parallel pilgrimage law attached to the House of 2:125.
Pleasing speech + God called as witness + fiercest disputer + land-corruption vs one who sells himself seeking God’s riḍwān. Classic hypocrite / sincere pair without the word munāfiq here.

Udkhulū fī l-silmi kāffatan. Silm can mean peace or Islam (the submission). Tafsir majority: enter Islam wholly. Level 1: enter the silm completely; do not follow Satan. If you slip after bayyināt, God is ʿazīz ḥakīm. Do they wait for God to come in canopies of cloud with angels — the matter is decided. Ask Banī Isrāʾīl how many a clear sign We gave them. Exchanging God’s blessing after it came: severe punishment.
Cloud-theophany language has biblical cousins (Exod 19; 24; 40; Dan 7). Here it is a warning against waiting for a spectacle instead of entering the silm.
2:212–214 world-adornment; one ummah; Garden not cheap

World-life is beautified for those who disbelieve; they mock the believers; muttaqūn will be above them on the Rising-Day. Mankind was one ummah; God sent prophets, mubashshirīn and mundhirīn, and sent down with them the Book with truth to judge in what they differed. Differing after knowledge is baghy. God guided the believers to the truth of that difference by His leave.

2:213 is a theory of revelation-history: original human unity → difference → prophets + Book as judge → further difference by the Book’s own recipients out of rivalry → God guides whom He wills. This is a load-bearing QRQ-0005 / 0010 verse.

2:214: you thought you would enter the Garden without the portion of those before you? They were touched by baʾsāʾ and ḍarrāʾ and shaken until messenger and believers said: when is God’s help? God’s help is near. Continuity of trial with prior communities.
sexual talk or act / iniquity / quarrel — in ihram
plain and sacred waymark of the hajj
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on pilgrimage + offering + days; different sanctuary and map
2:213 mankind one ummah then prophets and Book
REINTERPRETATION of sacred history vs Gen 11 / election of Israel as the main plot
2:214 Garden after shaking like those before
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with trial-of-the-faithful motif (Heb 11–12; Ps 22; Israel in the wilderness)
Severe in penalty; knows bounty-seeking; portion in both worlds; does not love corruption; guides whom He wills; help is near.
2:213 Book sent down with prophets to judge difference; 2:196–203 ritual attached to the House.
Hajj/umrah code; ihram bans; fidya menus.
Two prayers (world vs both worlds); sell the self for God's pleasure; enter silm wholly.
Difference after the Book is baghy; God then guides believers to the truth of the difference.
Hajj and umrah completed for God; prevention and tamattu rules
Arafat / mash'ar remembrance; two kinds of prayer
Enter the silm completely; do not wait for cloud-theophany
Mankind one ummah; prophets and Book to judge difference; difference after knowledge is baghy
Garden not entered without the shaking that hit those before

Ḥajj is legislated at the House already claimed for Abraham and Ishmael. Human history is told as original unity, then difference, then prophets and a judging Book, then rivalry among the Book’s recipients. The Garden is not a cheap door.
Next: 2:215–242 (spending, fighting orphans, wine/maysir first mention, menstruation, oaths, divorce — the family-law panel). May split 215–220 and 221–242 if thick.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP13 vv215-227
paragraphs: Why this cut: Spend / fight / wine / orphans / marriage / menses / oaths / īlāʾ. Full ṭalāq code is 2:228–237 and needs its own packet.

They ask what they should spend: parents, relatives, orphans, the poor, the traveler — whatever good you do God knows. Fighting is prescribed though you dislike it; you may hate what is good for you and love what is bad; God knows and you do not. They ask about fighting in the sacred month: great sin, but blocking from God’s way, kufr, and the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people is greater with God; fitnah is greater than killing. They will not cease fighting you until they turn you from your dīn if they can; whoever of you turns from his dīn and dies a kāfir — works are fruitless; those are companions of the Fire. Those who believed, emigrated, and struggled expect God’s mercy. They ask about wine and maysir: great sin and benefits for people; their sin is greater than their benefit. Spend the surplus (al-ʿafw). They ask about orphans: setting them right is best; if you mix with them they are your brothers; God knows the corrupter from the setter-right. Do not marry mushrik women until they believe; a believing slave-woman is better than a mushrik even if she pleases you. Do not marry mushrik men to your women until they believe; a believing slave is better than a mushrik even if he pleases you. Those call to the Fire; God calls to the Garden and forgiveness. They ask about menstruation: it is adhā; keep away from women in menstruation and do not approach until they are clean; when they have purified, come to them from where God has commanded. God loves those who repent often and those who purify themselves. Your women are a tilth; come to your tilth as you wish; send ahead for yourselves. Do not make God a target for your oaths against being pious, fearing, and putting things right among people. God will not take you to task for thoughtless oaths, but for what your hearts earned. Those who swear off their women wait four months; if they go back, God is forgiving; if they resolve on divorce, God hears and knows.
Same recipient list as 2:177’s gift-clause, minus freeing necks and those who ask. What you spend of good is known.

Fighting is kutiba though disliked. Sacred-month fighting is kabīr, but barring from God’s way, kufr in Him, the Sacred Mosque, and expelling its people is greater; fitnah is greater than killing. They will keep fighting you until they turn you from your dīn if they can. Apostasy-to-death: works void, Fire. Believers who emigrated and struggled hope for mercy.
Thickens 2:190–193. Sacred month is not an absolute shield when the other side’s conduct is framed as greater fitnah. Apostasy clause here is about dying in that state, not a penal code.
Great ithm and benefits; ithm greater than nafʿ. Not yet an absolute ban (5:90 will be). Spend the surplus.

QB-0051: PARTIAL AGREEMENT that wine can be a moral problem (Prov 20:1; 23:29–35; Eph 5:18) while wine is also used in biblical cult and blessing (Ps 104:15; John 2). Maysir is a local game of chance. This verse is graduated, not the later ḥadd regime.
Iṣlāḥ for them is best. Mixing affairs is allowed because they are brothers. God can tell corrupter from reformer. Continuity with 2:83, 2:177.

Do not marry mushrikāt until they believe; believing slave-woman is better than a pleasing mushrik. Reciprocal: do not give believing women to mushrikīn until they believe. They invite to the Fire; God invites to Garden and forgiveness.

5:5 will later permit chaste women of those given the Book. That later verse is not in this packet. Level 1 here is a mushrik-until-belief ban, both directions. People-of-the-Book exception is a later textual fact, not a silent clause in 2:221. QB-0052 vs Deut 7:3–4 / Ezra 9–10 (no covenant-marriage with the surrounding peoples): PARTIAL AGREEMENT on a faith-boundary for marriage. Different boundary-definition (mushrik vs the nations of Canaan / am ha-aretz).

Menstruation is adhā (harm / hurt / impurity-as-harm). Keep away; do not approach until they are clean; when they have purified, come from where God commanded. God loves tawwābīn and mutaṭahhirīn. Women are ḥarth (tilth); come to your tilth as you wish; send ahead.

QB-0053: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 15:19–24 (niddah separation). OMISSION of the seven-day count and object-impurity rules of Leviticus. “Come as you wish” to the tilth is a permission-clause about manner/timing after purity, not a license that cancels 2:222. Asbāb stories about a specific Jewish practice or a specific request are TAFSIR.

Do not use God as an ʿurḍa for oaths so as to avoid birr, taqwā, and iṣlāḥ among people. Laghw (thoughtless) oaths are not taken to account; what the hearts earned is. Īlāʾ (oath of sexual abstention from wives): four months. Return: God is forgiving. Resolve on ṭalāq: God hears and knows. This is the on-ramp to the divorce code.
QB-0054: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with oath-seriousness (Num 30; Deut 23:21–23; Matt 5:33–37). Matt 5 pushes toward not swearing; 2:224–225 regulates swearing and excuses laghw.
oath to abstain from one's wife
PARTIAL AGREEMENT that wine can be morally dangerous; this verse is not yet 5:90’s ban
No marriage to mushrikun until belief
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Deut 7 / Ezra on faith-bounded marriage; 5:5 Book-women not in this verse
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with Lev 15 niddah; shorter and without object-impurity code
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on binding speech; CONTRAST Matt 5: do-not-swear
Spend list; fighting prescribed; sacred-month calculus; wine/maysir weighted; orphan mixing; marriage boundary; menses; oaths; four-month ila'.
Surplus spending; islah for orphans; God loves tawwabin and mutatahhirin.
Spend on the near and weak; fighting prescribed though disliked
Sacred-month fight is kabir; fitnah and expulsion greater; apostasy-to-death
Khamr and maysir: sin greater than benefit; spend the surplus
No marriage to mushriks until they believe; believing slave better
Menstruation is adha; tilth permission after purity
Oaths: not a pretext against good; laghw excused; ila' four months

Ethics and household law arrive as answers to questions (yasʾalūnaka). Wine is weighted, not yet banned. Marriage is closed to mushrik partners until belief. Menses is harm requiring distance then return. Īlāʾ clocks four months toward either return or divorce.
Next: S002 CP14 = 2:228–242 (waiting period, divorce limits, nursing, widow-maintenance).

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP14 vv228-242
paragraphs: Divorced women wait three qurūʾ; they must not hide what God created in their wombs. Husbands have more right to return them in that period if they want iṣlāḥ. Women have the like of what is due from them with maʿrūf; men have a daraja over them. Ṭalāq is twice; then hold with maʿrūf or release with iḥsān. You may not take back what you gave them unless both fear they cannot keep God’s limits; then no blame in what she ransoms herself with (khulʿ). If he divorces her (third), she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband; if that one divorces her, no blame if they return if they think they can keep the limits. When you divorce women and they reach their term, hold them with maʿrūf or release with maʿrūf; do not hold them as harm to transgress. Whoever does that wrongs himself. Do not take God’s signs in mockery. When you divorce and they reach term, do not prevent them from remarrying their husbands if they agree with maʿrūf. That is purer for you. Mothers nurse two full years if the nursing is to be completed; the child’s father must provision and clothe the mother with maʿrūf; no soul is charged beyond its scope; no mother or father to be harmed because of the child; the heir has the like. Weaning by mutual consent: no blame. Hiring a wet-nurse: no blame if you hand over what you give with maʿrūf. Those of you who die and leave wives: the wives wait four months and ten; when they reach term, no blame on you for what they do with themselves with maʿrūf. No blame in alluding to a marriage proposal to women or keeping it inward, but do not make a secret pact except to speak a maʿrūf word; do not resolve the knot of marriage until the term is reached. There is no blame if you divorce women before touching them or assigning a farīḍa; assign them mutʿa — the well-off according to his means, the straitened according to his — a duty on the muḥsinīn. If you divorce before touching but after a farīḍa is assigned, then half of what you assigned unless they waive or he in whose hand is the marriage-knot waives; waiving is nearer to taqwā. Guard the prayers, especially the middle prayer; stand for God qānitīn. If you fear, then on foot or riding; when you are safe, remember God as He taught you what you did not know. Those of you who die and leave wives: a bequest for their wives of provision to a year without eviction; if they leave, no blame for what they do with themselves with maʿrūf. For the divorced: a provision with maʿrūf, a duty on the muttaqīn. Thus God makes clear His signs so that you may reason.

Three qurūʾ (purity-cycles or menses — the word is argued). Concealment of pregnancy forbidden. Husband’s return-right in the period if he wants reconciliation. Lahunna mithlu lladhī ʿalayhinna bi-l-maʿrūf — a reciprocity clause. Wa-li-l-rijāli ʿalayhinna darajatun — a degree. Both sentences are Level 1. Later fiqh loads “degree” with qiwāma from 4:34; do not import 4:34 yet.
2:229–232 twice, then third; do not block remarriage

Divorce is twice; then retain with maʿrūf or release with iḥsān. Taking back gifts is barred except khulʿ when both fear they cannot keep ḥudūd. After a third divorce she is not lawful until she marries another husband; if that marriage ends, return to the first is allowed if they think they can keep the limits. Hold or release at term with maʿrūf; holding as ḍirār is transgression. Do not prevent women from remarrying their (former) husbands when they agree with maʿrūf.

QB-0055 vs Deut 24:1–4: both are divorce-and-remarriage laws. Torah: if she marries another and that ends, she may not return to the first (it is tōʿēbāh). Quran 2:230: after the third ṭalāq she may not return to the first until she has married another; after that other marriage ends, return is allowed. That is an inversion of Deut 24’s final ban. PARTIAL AGREEMENT that divorce is a legal institution with limits; DIRECT CONTRAST on the intervening-marriage rule. Ṭalāq-twice-then-third is ADDITION relative to Deut 24’s simpler “bill of divorce.”

Two full years if completion is desired. Father’s duty: provision and clothing of the mother with maʿrūf. No soul charged beyond capacity. Neither parent harmed via the child. Heir carries a similar duty. Mutual weaning: no blame. Paid wet-nurse: no blame. This is child-maintenance law, not only ritual.

Four months and ten. After term, they may act with themselves with maʿrūf. Proposal by allusion is allowed; secret contract is not, except a maʿrūf word. Do not finalize marriage until the term ends. God knows what you hide.

Divorce before touch and before a named farīḍa: still give mutʿa according to means — duty on the muḥsinīn. If a farīḍa was named: half, unless she waives or he who holds the knot waives. Waiving is nearer taqwā. Do not forget bounty between you.
Guard the ṣalawāt and the middle prayer; stand qānitīn. Fear: pray walking or riding; when safe, remember God as He taught you. A cult-command dropped into family law — typical Baqarah texture.

Dying husbands: a waṣiyya of one year’s provision without eviction; if the widows leave, no blame. Divorced women: a provision with maʿrūf, duty on the muttaqīn. Relation of 2:240’s year to 2:234’s four-months-ten is a classic naskh debate (Level 4). Level 1: both sentences exist.
waiting units — menses or tuhr, argued
until she marries a husband other than him
PARTIAL AGREEMENT that divorce is regulated; CONTRAST: intervening marriage is a bar to return in Torah and a condition of return after third talaq in 2:230
ADDITION of numbered idda (3 quru'; 4 months 10 days). Torah widow law is levirate-centered (Deut 25), not this clock.
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with long nursing as a known Near Eastern norm; not a Bible-verse match
Idda; twice-then-third; khul'; nursing duties; widow clocks; mut'a; middle prayer; year-provision.
Ma'ruf / ihsan as the ethical floor of hold-or-release; waiving nearer taqwa.
Limits of God; knows what you hide; makes signs clear so you reason.
Three quru'; reciprocity with a male daraja; return if islah
Talaq twice then hold or release; third requires another marriage first
Do not block remarriage; nursing two years; father maintains
Widow 4 months 10 days; allusion ok; no knot until term
Mut'a for unconsummated divorce; middle prayer; year bequest vs 2:234 tension
DIRECT; naskh of 240 vs 234 is extra

Divorce is limited (twice, then a real intervening marriage), timed (qurūʾ / four-months-ten), and morally fenced (maʿrūf, not ḍirār). Recipro­city is stated and then a “degree” is stated. Deut 24 and 2:230 are the sharpest legal contrast in this panel: intervening marriage closes the door in the Torah and opens a door after a third ṭalāq here.

Next: 2:243–260 (those who left their homes, Ṭālūt / Saul, David and Goliath, God is the friend of those who believe, Abraham and the birds — comparison-heavy again). Then 2:261–286 closes the surah (spending, ribā, debt contract, 2:255 Āyat al-Kursī, last prayer of the Book).

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP15 vv243-260
paragraphs: Comparison: Saul / Gideon’s river / David–Goliath; Abraham’s argument; birds vs Gen 15

Have you not seen those who left their homes in thousands, fearing death? God said die; then He gave them life. Fight in God’s way; know God is hearing, knowing. Who will lend God a good loan so He multiplies it? The Children of Israel after Moses said to a prophet of theirs: raise up a king for us; we will fight in God’s way. He: if fighting is prescribed, might you not fight? They: why would we not fight when we have been expelled from our homes and our children? When fighting was prescribed, they turned away except a few. Their prophet: God has sent Ṭālūt as king. They: how can he have kingship over us when we are more worthy and he has not been given amplitude of wealth? He: God has chosen him and increased him in knowledge and body; God gives kingship to whom He wills. Their prophet: the sign of his kingship is that the ark will come to you, in it sakīna from your Lord and a remnant of what the house of Moses and the house of Aaron left, borne by angels. When Ṭālūt set out he said: God will test you with a river; whoever drinks of it is not of me, except a scoop with the hand. They drank except a few. When he and those who believed with him crossed, they said we have no power today against Jālūt and his troops. Those who thought they would meet God said: how many a small company has overcome a large one by God’s leave. When they went out against Jālūt they said: our Lord pour on us patience, make our feet firm, help us against the kāfir people. They routed them by God’s leave; Dāwūd killed Jālūt; God gave him kingship and ḥikmah and taught him of what He willed. If God did not repel people by means of one another the earth would be corrupted. These are God’s signs We recite to you in truth; you are of the messengers. Those messengers: We preferred some over others; among them are those to whom God spoke; He raised some in degrees; We gave Jesus son of Mary the bayyināt and supported him with rūḥ al-qudus. If God had willed, those after them would not have fought after clear proofs; but they differed — some believed, some disbelieved. Spend of what We provided before a day with no sale or friendship. Allāh: no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting; slumber and sleep do not take Him; His is what is in the heavens and the earth; who will intercede with Him except by His leave; He knows what is before them and behind them; they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills; His kursī extends over the heavens and the earth; preserving them does not tire Him; He is the Most High, the Tremendous. No compulsion in dīn; right has become distinct from error; whoever disbelieves in ṭāghūt and believes in God has grasped the firmest handhold. God is walī of those who believe; He brings them from darknesses to light; those who disbelieve, their awliyāʾ are ṭāghūt; they bring them from light to darknesses. Have you not seen the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord because God had given him kingship? Abraham: my Lord is He who gives life and death. He: I give life and death. Abraham: God brings the sun from the east; bring it from the west. The disbeliever was dumbfounded. Or like the one who passed by a town collapsed on its roofs: how will God give life to this after its death? God made him die a hundred years then raised him. How long have you tarried? A day or part of a day. No: a hundred years. Look at your food and drink — it has not spoiled — and at your donkey; We make you a sign; look at the bones how We raise them then clothe them with flesh. When it was clear to him he said: I know God is over all things able. When Abraham said: my Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. Have you not believed? Yes, but that my heart be at rest. Take four birds, incline them to you, then put on each mountain a portion of them, then call them; they will come to you in haste.
Thousands leave homes fearing death; God says die, then revives. Often read as a plague-or-jihad parable. Level 1 is the revival-after-command. Good loan to God: spend-theology heading into 2:261.

After Moses, Israel asks a prophet for a king to fight. They promise; when fighting is written they turn away except a few. God sends Ṭālūt. They object: we have more right; he lacks wealth. Answer: God chose him and increased him in knowledge and body. Sign: the tābūt (ark) will come, in it sakīna and a remnant of Moses’ and Aaron’s house, carried by angels. River test: drink and you are not of me, except a handful. Most drink. The remnant crosses; some panic at Jālūt; the certain say a small company can beat a large one by leave. Prayer for ṣabr and thabāt. Dāwūd kills Jālūt; God gives him mulk and ḥikmah.

QB-0058 Saul: 1 Sam 8–10 Israel asks Samuel for a king; God grants Saul; objection-themes exist (tribe of Benjamin, not Judah). The Quranic wealth-objection and “increased in body” match Saul’s stature in 1 Sam 9–10 more than his later fall. The ark as sign of kingship is a rearrangement: in 1 Sam 4–7 the ark is lost and returned before Saul; here it arrives as Ṭālūt’s credential.
QB-0059 River test: that scene in the HB is Gideon (Judg 7:4–7), not Saul. The Quran attaches a Gideon-shaped filter to Ṭālūt. ADDITION / RELOCATION of a motif.

QB-0060 David and Goliath: 1 Sam 17. AGREEMENT that David kills the champion and later has kingship. OMISSION of sling detail, Jesse, the forty days, Goliath’s armor speech. Ḥikmah / teaching is extra relative to that chapter (HB David’s “wisdom” is a later court-and-psalm profile).
Prophet of 2:246 is unnamed (Samuel in the HB). Jalūt = Goliath. Tālūt is the received Arabic for Saul.

Some messengers preferred; some God spoke to; some raised in degrees. Jesus son of Mary: bayyināt and rūḥ al-qudus — same pair as 2:87. If God had willed those after them would not have fought after the proofs; they differed. Append to the Jesus dossier as sequential hit #3 in this surah.

The Living, the Self-Subsisting; no slumber; ownership of heavens and earth; intercession only by leave; knowledge unbounded except what He wills; the kursī extends over heavens and earth; preserving them does not tire Him. This is the surah’s densest tawhid paragraph. QI-0002 (intercession) is now explicit: illā bi-idhnihi.

Lā ikrāha fī l-dīn. Right is distinct from error. Whoever rejects ṭāghūt and believes in God has the firmest handhold. God is walī of the believers (darkness to light); ṭāghūt are awliyāʾ of the disbelievers (light to darkness). How 2:256 sits with fighting verses already logged is a live tension inside the surah — record, do not flatten. Later naskh claims that 2:256 is cancelled by the sword verse are Level 4.
A king argues with Abraham: I give life and death. Abraham moves the question to the sun’s east. The interlocutor is unnamed (tafsir: Nimrod).
A man passes a ruined town; dies a hundred years; food has not spoiled; donkey bones are recomposed. Unnamed.
Abraham asks how God gives life to the dead; not from unbelief but li-yaṭmaʾinna qalbī. Four birds, made to incline, portioned on mountains, called, come in haste.

QB-0061: Gen 15 is Abraham cutting animals and a smoking firepot passing between pieces — a covenant rite, not a reconstitution-of-birds lesson. Similar toolkit (Abraham + birds/animals + divine life-power), different plot. Ezekiel 37 (bones clothed with flesh) is closer to 2:259’s donkey/town than to 2:260. POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP of motifs; not identity of narrative.
false objects of loyalty / idols / rebel powers
incline / train / cut — sense argued for the birds
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with 1 Sam 8–10; ark-as-sign is rearranged
AGREEMENT on the kill + later kingship; OMISSION of 1 Sam 17 detail
Abraham and birds / town of bones
POSSIBLE RELATIONSHIP to Gen 15 toolkit and Ezek 37; different plots
Thousands die by command and are revived; good loan
Talut, ark, river test, David kills Jalut
2:253 Jesus bayyinat and ruh al-qudus; messengers ranked
Ayat al-Kursi; intercession only by leave
No compulsion in din; God wali of believers
Abraham vs the king; hundred-year town; four birds

Israel’s king-story is retold with a Gideon filter on Saul and a short David-kills-Goliath line. Jesus is again Spirit-supported. God is the Living whose kursī holds the heavens; dīn is not by compulsion in 2:256’s wording. Abraham is shown how the dead live.
Next / last Baqarah packets: 2:261–281 (spend, ribā, the debt contract) then 2:282–286 (or 2:261–286 as close). Āyat al-Kursī is in this packet already.

packets.title: S002 Al-Baqarah CP16 vv261-286
paragraphs: Those who spend in God’s way are like a grain that grows seven ears of a hundred grains; God multiplies for whom He wills. Spending followed by reminder-of-favor or injury has no reward; kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. Do not void your ṣadaqāt with mann and adhā. God does not guide the kāfir. Spending to be seen vs spending seeking God’s face — a garden on a height, rain, double yield vs a hard rock. The devil promises poverty and commands indecency; God promises forgiveness and bounty. Whatever you spend of good is for yourselves, seeking God’s face; it will be repaid in full. Charity to the poor who are constrained in God’s way, whom the ignorant think rich because of restraint — you know them by their mark; they do not ask people importunately. Those who spend night and day, secretly and openly: no fear, no grief. Those who eat ribā do not stand except as one whom Satan batters with touch, because they say sale is like ribā. God permitted sale and forbade ribā. Whoever takes the admonition and desists: what is past is his; his affair is with God. Whoever returns: Fire, abiding. God destroys ribā and increases ṣadaqāt. Those who believe, do ṣāliḥāt, pray, give zakāt: reward, no fear, no grief. O believers, fear God and give up remaining ribā if you are believers. If you do not, take notice of war from God and His messenger; if you repent you have your capitals; you do not wrong and are not wronged. If the debtor is in difficulty, respite until ease; that you give it as charity is better. Guard yourselves against a day you return to God; every soul is paid what it earned. When you contract a debt for a named term, write it. A scribe writes with justice; he may not refuse. The debtor dictates; if he cannot, his walī dictates. Two male witnesses; if not two men, a man and two women from those you accept as witnesses, so that if one of the two women errs the other reminds her. Witnesses may not refuse. Do not tire of writing it, small or large. Immediate hand-to-hand trade need not be written; take witnesses when you trade. Do not harm scribe or witness. If you are on a journey and find no scribe, a taken pledge. If one of you trusts another, let the trusted discharge his trust. Conceal not testimony; whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful. To God belongs what is in the heavens and the earth; whether you show what is in yourselves or hide it, God will call you to account; He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. The messenger believed in what was sent down to him from his Lord, and the believers; each believed in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers — we make no distinction between any of His messengers. They said: we hear and we obey; Your forgiveness, our Lord; to You is the becoming. God does not charge a soul except its capacity; it has what it earned and against it what it earned. Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or err. Our Lord, do not lay on us a burden as You laid on those before us. Our Lord, do not lay on us what we have no strength for. Pardon us, forgive us, have mercy on us. You are our Mawlā; help us against the kāfir people.

Multiplication image (7×100). Voiding charity by reminder and injury. Kind word better than wounded gift. Two gardens: height-with-rain vs rock-with-dust. Constrained poor who do not beg hard. Night/day, secret/open spenders get the 2:38 cadence again (no fear, no grief). Devil’s counter-promise: poverty.

Eaters of ribā stand like one touched by Satan. Their slogan: sale is like ribā. God permitted bayʿ and forbade ribā. Past amounts kept if one desists; return to it is Fire. God destroys ribā and grows ṣadaqāt. Give up remaining ribā; otherwise war from God and His messenger. Capitals only; no wringing. Hardship: respite; better to remit as charity. Then the return-day.

QB-0062: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with biblical hostility to interest on a brother (Exod 22:25; Lev 25:35–37; Deut 23:19–20 allows interest to a foreigner). Ezekiel 18 lists neshekh among sins. NT: Luke 6:34–35 push toward giving without expecting return. The Quranic war-notice and sale-is-not-ribā distinction are ADDITION relative to Torah’s brother/foreigner split. What counts as ribā in later fiqh is not this verse’s job.

Longest verse in the Quran. Write term-debts. Just scribe; debtor dictates; walī if needed. Witnesses: two men, or one man and two women from acceptable witnesses, so that if one woman errs the other reminds. Purpose clause is reminder, not a metaphysics of intellect. Hand-to-hand spot trade may skip writing. Travel: pledge. Trust: discharge it. Do not conceal testimony.

QB-0063: PARTIAL AGREEMENT with biblical insistence on honest weights, witnesses, and not perverting justice (Deut 19:15 two or three witnesses; Lev 19:13 wages). Two-women-for-one-man in this commercial-witness slot has no exact Torah twin. Later polemical use of 2:282 as a global statement about women is wider than the verse’s stated purpose (tadhkīr if one errs).

Hidden and shown inner states will be accounted; God forgives or punishes whom He wills. Creed: God, angels, books, messengers; no distinction among messengers; we hear and obey — the inversion of 2:93’s hear-and-disobey. God does not charge a soul beyond its wusʿ. The last prayer: forgetfulness and error; do not load us as You loaded those before; do not load what we cannot bear; ʿafw, ghufrān, raḥma; You are our Mawlā; help against the kāfir people.

“Those before us” in the burden-clause is often read as Israel’s law-load (cf. 2:286 with 7:157 / 4:160). Level 1: a prior community was given a heavier burden; this ummah asks not to repeat it. That is a continuity-and-relief claim toward QRQ-0003 / 0007.
reminder of favor / injury that voids charity
increase / usury / interest — scope argued in fiqh
notice of war from God and His messenger
Riba ban vs Torah interest rules
PARTIAL AGREEMENT on hostility to interest toward the in-group; ADDITION of war-notice and sale≠riba slogan-refutation; Torah allows neshekh to a foreigner
PARTIAL AGREEMENT with two-or-three-witness justice culture; two-women clause is ADDITION with a stated reminder purpose
Hear and obey vs 2:93 hear and disobey
This close inverts the calf-generation formula
Spend multiplied; do not void charity with reminder and injury
Riba forbidden; sale permitted; remaining riba = war notice; respite for hardship
Write term-debts; two men or one man and two women as witnesses
Creed of 2:285; no soul charged beyond capacity; closing prayer 2:286

Al-Baqarah opened with the Book as guidance for the muttaqīn and closed with a community that hears and obeys, asks not to be loaded as those before were loaded, and takes God as Mawlā. Between those poles: Adam, Israel’s saga, Jesus named, Abraham’s House, qibla, naskh, ḥajj, family law, Ṭālūt, the Living whose kursī holds the world, and a market ethic that bans ribā and commands ink.
Next surah in canonical order: S003 Āl ʿImrān — Mary, Zechariah, the family of ʿImrān, and a thicker Jesus file. Propose first packet 3:1–32 or 3:1–20 depending on verse volume.

pickthall.name: The Meaning of the Glorious Koran

verses.arabic: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ الٓمٓ
verses.itani: Alif, Lam, Meem.
verses.pickthall: Alif. Lam. Mim.

verses.arabic: ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ لَا رَيْبَ ۛ فِيهِ ۛ هُدًۭى لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ
verses.itani: This is the Book in which there is no doubt, a guide for the righteous.
verses.pickthall: This is the Scripture whereof there is no doubt, a guidance unto those who ward off (evil).

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْغَيْبِ وَيُقِيمُونَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ يُنفِقُونَ
verses.itani: Those who believe in the unseen, and perform the prayers, and give from what We have provided for them.
verses.pickthall: Who believe in the Unseen, and establish worship, and spend of that We have bestowed upon them;

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبْلِكَ وَبِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمْ يُوقِنُونَ
verses.itani: And those who believe in what was revealed to you, and in what was revealed before you, and are certain of the Hereafter.
verses.pickthall: And who believe in that which is revealed unto thee (Muhammad) and that which was revealed before thee, and are certain of the Hereafter.

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ عَلَىٰ هُدًۭى مِّن رَّبِّهِمْ ۖ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْلِحُونَ
verses.itani: These are upon guidance from their Lord. These are the successful.
verses.pickthall: These depend on guidance from their Lord. These are the successful.

verses.arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيْهِمْ ءَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ أَمْ لَمْ تُنذِرْهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ
verses.itani: As for those who disbelieve—it is the same for them, whether you have warned them, or have not warned them—they do not believe.
verses.pickthall: As for the Disbelievers, Whether thou warn them or thou warn them not it is all one for them; they believe not.

verses.arabic: خَتَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَعَلَىٰ سَمْعِهِمْ ۖ وَعَلَىٰٓ أَبْصَٰرِهِمْ غِشَٰوَةٌۭ ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: God has set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing, and over their vision is a veil. They will have a severe torment.
verses.pickthall: Allah hath sealed their hearing and their hearts, and on their eyes there is a covering. Theirs will be an awful doom.

verses.arabic: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَقُولُ ءَامَنَّا بِٱللَّهِ وَبِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَمَا هُم بِمُؤْمِنِينَ
verses.itani: Among the people are those who say, “We believe in God and in the Last Day,” but they are not believers.
verses.pickthall: And of mankind are some who say: We believe in Allah and the Last Day, when they believe not.

verses.arabic: يُخَٰدِعُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَمَا يَخْدَعُونَ إِلَّآ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.itani: They seek to deceive God and those who believe, but they deceive none but themselves, though they are not aware.
verses.pickthall: They think to beguile Allah and those who believe, and they beguile none save themselves; but they perceive not.

verses.arabic: فِى قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌۭ فَزَادَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مَرَضًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ
verses.itani: In their hearts is sickness, and God has increased their sickness. They will have a painful punishment because of their denial.
verses.pickthall: In their hearts is a disease, and Allah increaseth their disease. A painful doom is theirs because they lie.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ لَا تُفْسِدُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُصْلِحُونَ
verses.itani: And when it is said to them, “Do not make trouble on earth,” they say, “We are only reformers.”
verses.pickthall: And when it is said unto them: Make not mischief in the earth, they say: We are peacemakers only.

verses.arabic: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُفْسِدُونَ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَشْعُرُونَ
verses.itani: In fact, they are the troublemakers, but they are not aware.
verses.pickthall: Are not they indeed the mischief-makers? But they perceive not.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ ءَامِنُوا۟ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلنَّاسُ قَالُوٓا۟ أَنُؤْمِنُ كَمَآ ءَامَنَ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ ۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ وَلَٰكِن لَّا يَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: And when it is said to them, “Believe as the people have believed,” they say, “Shall we believe as the fools have believed?” In fact, it is they who are the fools, but they do not know.
verses.pickthall: And when it is said unto them: believe as the people believe, they say: shall we believe as the foolish believe? are not they indeed the foolish? But they know not.

verses.arabic: وَإِذَا لَقُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ قَالُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ شَيَٰطِينِهِمْ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ مُسْتَهْزِءُونَ
verses.itani: And when they come across those who believe, they say, “We believe”; but when they are alone with their devils, they say, “We are with you; we were only ridiculing.”
verses.pickthall: And when they fall in with those who believe, they say: We believe; but when they go apart to their devils they declare: Lo! we are with you; verily we did but mock.

verses.arabic: ٱللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ وَيَمُدُّهُمْ فِى طُغْيَٰنِهِمْ يَعْمَهُونَ
verses.itani: It is God who ridicules them, and leaves them bewildered in their transgression.
verses.pickthall: Allah (Himself) doth mock them, leaving them to wander blindly on in their contumacy.

verses.arabic: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱشْتَرَوُا۟ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةَ بِٱلْهُدَىٰ فَمَا رَبِحَت تِّجَٰرَتُهُمْ وَمَا كَانُوا۟ مُهْتَدِينَ
verses.itani: Those are they who have bartered error for guidance; but their trade does not profit them, and they are not guided.
verses.pickthall: These are they who purchase error at the price of guidance, so their commerce doth not prosper, neither are they guided.

verses.arabic: مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ ٱلَّذِى ٱسْتَوْقَدَ نَارًۭا فَلَمَّآ أَضَآءَتْ مَا حَوْلَهُۥ ذَهَبَ ٱللَّهُ بِنُورِهِمْ وَتَرَكَهُمْ فِى ظُلُمَٰتٍۢ لَّا يُبْصِرُونَ
verses.itani: Their likeness is that of a person who kindled a fire; when it illuminated all around him, God took away their light, and left them in darkness, unable to see.
verses.pickthall: Their likeness is as the likeness of one who kindleth fire, and when it sheddeth its light around him Allah taketh away their light and leaveth them in darkness, where they cannot see,

verses.arabic: صُمٌّۢ بُكْمٌ عُمْىٌۭ فَهُمْ لَا يَرْجِعُونَ
verses.itani: Deaf, dumb, blind. They will not return.
verses.pickthall: Deaf, dumb and blind; and they return not.

verses.arabic: أَوْ كَصَيِّبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فِيهِ ظُلُمَٰتٌۭ وَرَعْدٌۭ وَبَرْقٌۭ يَجْعَلُونَ أَصَٰبِعَهُمْ فِىٓ ءَاذَانِهِم مِّنَ ٱلصَّوَٰعِقِ حَذَرَ ٱلْمَوْتِ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ مُحِيطٌۢ بِٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.itani: Or like a cloudburst from the sky, in which is darkness, and thunder, and lightning. They press their fingers into their ears from the thunderbolts, in fear of death. But God surrounds the disbelievers.
verses.pickthall: Or like a rainstorm from the sky, wherein is darkness, thunder and the flash of lightning. They thrust their fingers in their ears by reason of the thunder-claps, for fear of death, Allah encompasseth the disbelievers (in His guidance, His omniscience and His omnipotence).

verses.arabic: يَكَادُ ٱلْبَرْقُ يَخْطَفُ أَبْصَٰرَهُمْ ۖ كُلَّمَآ أَضَآءَ لَهُم مَّشَوْا۟ فِيهِ وَإِذَآ أَظْلَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ قَامُوا۟ ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَذَهَبَ بِسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
verses.itani: The lightning almost snatches their sight away. Whenever it illuminates for them, they walk in it; but when it grows dark over them, they stand still. Had God willed, He could have taken away their hearing and their sight. God is capable of everything.
verses.pickthall: The lightning almost snatcheth away their sight from them. As often as it flasheth forth for them they walk therein, and when it darkeneth against them they stand still. If Allah willed, He could destroy their hearing and their sight. Lo! Allah is able to do all things.

verses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكُمْ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
verses.itani: O people! Worship your Lord who created you and those before you, that you may attain piety.
verses.pickthall: O mankind! worship your Lord, Who hath created you and those before you, so that ye may ward off (evil).

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ فِرَٰشًۭا وَٱلسَّمَآءَ بِنَآءًۭ وَأَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَخْرَجَ بِهِۦ مِنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ رِزْقًۭا لَّكُمْ ۖ فَلَا تَجْعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ أَندَادًۭا وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: He who made the earth a habitat for you, and the sky a structure, and sends water down from the sky, and brings out fruits thereby, as a sustenance for you. Therefore, do not assign rivals to God while you know.
verses.pickthall: Who hath appointed the earth a resting-place for you, and the sky a canopy; and causeth water to pour down from the sky, thereby producing fruits as food for you. And do not set up rivals to Allah when ye know (better).

verses.arabic: وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍۢ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.itani: And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to Our servant, then produce a chapter like these, and call your witnesses apart from God, if you are truthful.
verses.pickthall: And if ye are in doubt concerning that which We reveal unto Our slave (Muhammad), then produce a surah of the like thereof, and call your witness beside Allah if ye are truthful.

verses.arabic: فَإِن لَّمْ تَفْعَلُوا۟ وَلَن تَفْعَلُوا۟ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱلنَّارَ ٱلَّتِى وَقُودُهَا ٱلنَّاسُ وَٱلْحِجَارَةُ ۖ أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.itani: But if you do not—and you will not—then beware the Fire whose fuel is people and stones, prepared for the disbelievers.
verses.pickthall: And if ye do it not - and ye can never do it - then guard yourselves against the Fire prepared for disbelievers, whose fuel is of men and stones.

verses.arabic: وَبَشِّرِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَمِلُوا۟ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ جَنَّٰتٍۢ تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۖ كُلَّمَا رُزِقُوا۟ مِنْهَا مِن ثَمَرَةٍۢ رِّزْقًۭا ۙ قَالُوا۟ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِى رُزِقْنَا مِن قَبْلُ ۖ وَأُتُوا۟ بِهِۦ مُتَشَٰبِهًۭا ۖ وَلَهُمْ فِيهَآ أَزْوَٰجٌۭ مُّطَهَّرَةٌۭ ۖ وَهُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.itani: And give good news to those who believe and do righteous deeds; that they will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. Whenever they are provided with fruit therefrom as sustenance, they will say, “This is what we were provided with before,” and they will be given the like of it. And they will have pure spouses therein, and they will abide therein forever.
verses.pickthall: And give glad tidings (O Muhammad) unto those who believe and do good works; that theirs are Gardens underneath which rivers flow; as often as they are regaled with food of the fruit thereof, they say: this is what was given us aforetime; and it is given to them in resemblance. There for them are pure companions; there for ever they abide.

verses.arabic: ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْىِۦٓ أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًۭا مَّا بَعُوضَةًۭ فَمَا فَوْقَهَا ۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ ۖ وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَآ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًۭا ۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِۦ كَثِيرًۭا وَيَهْدِى بِهِۦ كَثِيرًۭا ۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِۦٓ إِلَّا ٱلْفَٰسِقِينَ
verses.itani: God does not shy away from making an example of a gnat, or something above it. As for those who believe, they know that it is the Truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, “What did God intend by this example?” He leads astray many thereby, and He guides many thereby; but He misleads thereby only the evildoers.
verses.pickthall: Lo! Allah disdaineth not to coin the similitude even of a gnat. Those who believe know that it is the truth from their Lord; but those who disbelieve say: What doth Allah wish (to teach) by such a similitude? He misleadeth many thereby, and He guideth many thereby; and He misleadeth thereby only miscreants;

verses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرُونَ
verses.itani: Those who violate God’s covenant after its confirmation, and sever what God has commanded to be joined, and commit evil on earth. These are the losers.
verses.pickthall: Those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah ordered to be joined, and (who) make mischief in the earth: Those are they who are the losers.

verses.arabic: كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَكُنتُمْ أَمْوَٰتًۭا فَأَحْيَٰكُمْ ۖ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ
verses.itani: How can you deny God, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will put you to death, then He will bring you to life, then to Him you will be returned?
verses.pickthall: How disbelieve ye in Allah when ye were dead and He gave life to you! Then He will give you death, then life again, and then unto Him ye will return.

verses.arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَ لَكُم مَّا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًۭا ثُمَّ ٱسْتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
verses.itani: It is He who created for you everything on earth, then turned to the heaven, and made them seven heavens. And He is aware of all things.
verses.pickthall: He it is Who created for you all that is in the earth. Then turned He to the heaven, and fashioned it as seven heavens. And He is knower of all things.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّى جَاعِلٌۭ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةًۭ ۖ قَالُوٓا۟ أَتَجْعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفْسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسْفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: When your Lord said to the angels, “I am placing a successor on earth.” They said, “Will You place in it someone who will cause corruption in it and shed blood, while we declare Your praises and sanctify You?” He said, “I know what you do not know.”
verses.pickthall: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not.

verses.arabic: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلْأَسْمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِى بِأَسْمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.itani: And He taught Adam the names, all of them; then he presented them to the angels, and said, “Tell Me the names of these, if you are sincere.”
verses.pickthall: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful.

verses.arabic: قَالُوا۟ سُبْحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلْمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمْتَنَآ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلْعَلِيمُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
verses.itani: They said, “Glory be to You! We have no knowledge except what You have taught us. It is you who are the Knowledgeable, the Wise.”
verses.pickthall: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise.

verses.arabic: قَالَ يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ أَنۢبِئْهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ ۖ فَلَمَّآ أَنۢبَأَهُم بِأَسْمَآئِهِمْ قَالَ أَلَمْ أَقُل لَّكُمْ إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَأَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا كُنتُمْ تَكْتُمُونَ
verses.itani: He said, “O Adam, tell them their names.” And when he told them their names, He said, “Did I not tell you that I know the secrets of the heavens and the earth, and that I know what you reveal and what you conceal?”
verses.pickthall: He said: O Adam! Inform them of their names, and when he had informed them of their names, He said: Did I not tell you that I know the secret of the heavens and the earth? And I know that which ye disclose and which ye hide.

verses.arabic: وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِءَادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
verses.itani: And We said to the angels, “Bow down to Adam.” They bowed down, except for Satan. He refused, was arrogant, and was one of the disbelievers.
verses.pickthall: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever.

verses.arabic: وَقُلْنَا يَٰٓـَٔادَمُ ٱسْكُنْ أَنتَ وَزَوْجُكَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا وَلَا تَقْرَبَا هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةَ فَتَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
verses.itani: We said, “O Adam, inhabit the Garden, you and your spouse, and eat from it freely as you please, but do not approach this tree, lest you become wrongdoers.”
verses.pickthall: And We said: O Adam! Dwell thou and thy wife in the Garden, and eat ye freely (of the fruits) thereof where ye will; but come not nigh this tree lest ye become wrong-doers.

verses.arabic: فَأَزَلَّهُمَا ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ عَنْهَا فَأَخْرَجَهُمَا مِمَّا كَانَا فِيهِ ۖ وَقُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ بَعْضُكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّۭ ۖ وَلَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُسْتَقَرٌّۭ وَمَتَٰعٌ إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
verses.itani: But Satan caused them to slip from it, and caused them to depart the state they were in. We said, “Go down, some of you enemies of one another. And you will have residence on earth, and enjoyment for a while.”
verses.pickthall: But Satan caused them to deflect therefrom and expelled them from the (happy) state in which they were; and We said: Fall down, one of you a foe unto the other! There shall be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a time.

verses.arabic: فَتَلَقَّىٰٓ ءَادَمُ مِن رَّبِّهِۦ كَلِمَٰتٍۢ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلتَّوَّابُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
verses.itani: Then Adam received words from his Lord, so He relented towards him. He is the Relenting, the Merciful.
verses.pickthall: Then Adam received from his Lord words (of revelation), and He relented toward him. Lo! He is the relenting, the Merciful.

verses.arabic: قُلْنَا ٱهْبِطُوا۟ مِنْهَا جَمِيعًۭا ۖ فَإِمَّا يَأْتِيَنَّكُم مِّنِّى هُدًۭى فَمَن تَبِعَ هُدَاىَ فَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ
verses.itani: We said, “Go down from it, all of you. Yet whenever guidance comes to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance—they have nothing to fear, nor shall they grieve.
verses.pickthall: We said: Go down, all of you, from hence; but verily there cometh unto you from Me a guidance; and whoso followeth My guidance, there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve.

verses.arabic: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَكَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَآ أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلنَّارِ ۖ هُمْ فِيهَا خَٰلِدُونَ
verses.itani: But as for those who disbelieve and reject Our signs—these are the inmates of the Fire—wherein they will remain forever.”
verses.pickthall: But they who disbelieve, and deny Our revelations, such are rightful Peoples of the Fire. They will abide therein.

verses.arabic: يَٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِىٓ أُوفِ بِعَهْدِكُمْ وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱرْهَبُونِ
verses.itani: O Children of Israel! Remember My blessings which I bestowed upon you, and fulfill your pledge to Me, and I will fulfill My pledge to you, and fear Me.
verses.pickthall: O Children of Israel! Remember My favour wherewith I favoured you, and fulfil your (part of the) covenant, I shall fulfil My (part of the) covenant, and fear Me.

verses.arabic: وَءَامِنُوا۟ بِمَآ أَنزَلْتُ مُصَدِّقًۭا لِّمَا مَعَكُمْ وَلَا تَكُونُوٓا۟ أَوَّلَ كَافِرٍۭ بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِى ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًۭا وَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱتَّقُونِ
verses.itani: And believe in what I revealed, confirming what is with you; and do not be the first to deny it; and do not exchange My revelations for a small price; and be conscious of Me.
verses.pickthall: And believe in that which I reveal, confirming that which ye possess already (of the Scripture), and be not first to disbelieve therein, and part not with My revelations for a trifling price, and keep your duty unto Me.

verses.arabic: وَلَا تَلْبِسُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ بِٱلْبَٰطِلِ وَتَكْتُمُوا۟ ٱلْحَقَّ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
verses.itani: And do not mix truth with falsehood, and do not conceal the truth while you know.
verses.pickthall: Confound not truth with falsehood, nor knowingly conceal the truth.

verses.arabic: وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱرْكَعُوا۟ مَعَ ٱلرَّٰكِعِينَ
